## BioCatch

Connector ID (`connector.id` in the resource): `biocatchConnector`

Properties (used under the `properties` block in the resource as a key in the JSON object):

* `accountBalance` (string): The user's account balance prior to making this monetary activity. Console display name: "".
* `accountID` (string): Unique identifier of the user at the customer side across different accounts. Console display name: "".
* `accountOpenDate` (string): The date the account was opened. Console display name: "".
* `activityAmount` (string): The amount associated with a movement of money. Console display name: "".
* `activityAmountTotal` (string): The total amount associated with the transaction. Console display name: "".
* `activityCategory` (string): Select Activity Category to see a list of supported activity types below. Console display name: "".
* `activityName` (string): The name of the activity that will give a better indication to what is the activity. Console display name: "".
* `activityType` (string): The type of activity for which scoring is requested. Please select the activity category first. Console display name: "".
* `apiUrl` (string): Console display name: "".
* `authMethodUsed` (string): Console display name: "".
* `authenticationResult` (string): Indication how user’s external authentication ended. Console display name: "".
* `biocatchAction` (string): Console display name: "".
* `biocatchFraudType` (string): BioCatch Fraud Type. Console display name: "".
* `biocatchSessionResult` (string): Console display name: "".
* `biocatchSessionStatus` (string): Console display name: "".
* `biometricLogin` (string): An indication the user used biometric authentication in order to access the application. Console display name: "".
* `brand` (string): The related session brand. Console display name: "".
* `cardType` (string): Console display name: "".
* `cellularAreaNumbers` (string): The user’s cell area code. Console display name: "".
* `comment` (string): Additional comment. The maximum length is 200 alphanumeric characters. Console display name: "Comment".
* `contextName` (string): Setting a contextName before each page/screen in the user journey is invoked will help BioCatch find behavioral trends. Console display name: "".
* `customFraudType` (string): Lets customers send additional information/values not included in fraudType above. The maximum length is 200 alphanumeric characters. Console display name: "Custom Fraud Type".
* `customerId` (string): Console display name: "".
* `customerPassword` (string): The BioCatch password if used as part of the authentication process. For more information, refer to the Get Started/Authentic action section. Console display name: "".
* `customerSessionId` (string): Customer Session ID for the session. Console display name: "".
* `dateOfCreation` (string): The date of the account/merchant was created. Console display name: "".
* `deviceID` (string): The user's browser. Console display name: "".
* `deviceIpStatus` (string): Indication provided by the customer if the device and/or IP are known to the customer. Console display name: "".
* `deviceModel` (string): An indication provided by the customer to the device model used by the user. Console display name: "".
* `income` (string): The user’s annual income. Console display name: "".
* `invoiceNumber` (string): The invoice number to allow connecting between different payments for the same invoice. Console display name: "".
* `isLoginSuccess` (string): An indication of what point in the login process a request is sent. Console display name: "".
* `javascriptCdnUrl` (string): Console display name: "".
* `jobDescription` (string): The user's job FP/IP category. The user’s annual income. Console display name: "".
* `language` (string): The language the user is using in the website. Recommended for PSD2/Open Banking/Score at login. Console display name: "".
* `lastWithdrawalAmount` (string): The amount used as part of the last withdrawal from this account. Console display name: "".
* `lastWithdrawalDate` (string): The last withdrawal date from this account. Console display name: "".
* `loadingText` (string): Console display name: "Initialization Loading text".
* `maritalStatus` (string): The user's relationship with a significant other. Console display name: "".
* `market` (string): Different area business is conducted. Console display name: "".
* `membershipID` (string): The user's membership ID. Console display name: "".
* `numOfFailedAuth` (string): An indication to the number of authentication attempts that were done so far, and user failed. Console display name: "".
* `onlineAccountOpenDate` (string): The date the online account was opened. Console display name: "".
* `passwordChangeDate` (string): The date of the last password change. Console display name: "".
* `payeeAccountType` (string): The type of the payee account. Console display name: "".
* `payeeAge` (string): The age of the payee account provided by the customer. Console display name: "".
* `payeeValue` (string): An anonymized value or associated key if the activity has a payee or beneficiary. Console display name: "".
* `payerAccountType` (string): The type of the payee account. Console display name: "".
* `payerValue` (string): Console display name: "".
* `paymentMethod` (string): The payment method used by the user. Console display name: "".
* `permissionsRequested` (string): The permissions that the user requested for the AISP flow. Recommended for PSD2/Open Banking. Console display name: "".
* `platformType` (string): Provide indication in which platform user is performing the activity. Console display name: "".
* `postcode` (string): The user’s home postcode. Console display name: "".
* `product` (string): The type of product the user is using on customer side. Console display name: "".
* `recurrentPayee` (string): An indication we have multiple payments to the same payee over time. Console display name: "".
* `sdkToken` (string): Console display name: "".
* `serviceCategory` (string): The product/service category selected by the user in the PISP flow. Recommended for PSD2/Open Banking. Console display name: "".
* `sessionType` (string): Denotation for different types of sessions such as user, admin, or test. Console display name: "".
* `shipmentCountry` (string): The destination country of the shipment selected by the user in PISP flow. Recommended for PSD2/Open Banking. Console display name: "".
* `shipmentType` (string): The type of shipment selected by the user in PISP flow. Recommended for PSD2/Open Banking. Console display name: "".
* `solution` (string): An indication to which BioCatch solution customer is using. Console display name: "Solution".
* `thirdPartyFlow` (string): The flow that the session is originating from. Recommended for PSD2/Open Banking. Console display name: "".
* `timeOut` (string): The maximum number of milliseconds to wait before returning a score. BioCatch will use this number to decide whether to calculate a score or return a score from the cache (in case action=getScore) . If not specified, the system default is used. Console display name: "".
* `timestamp` (string): Session Timestamp. Console display name: "Timestamp".
* `transactionID` (string): A unique identifier to transaction sent by the customer. Console display name: "".
* `truthApiKey` (string): Fraudulent/Genuine Session Reporting API Key. Console display name: "".
* `truthApiUrl` (string): Fraudulent/Genuine Session Reporting. Console display name: "".
* `userType` (string): An indication for the type of user performing this activity. Console display name: "".
* `uuid` (string): Unique User ID. Console display name: "UUID".
* `web_journey` (string): An indication what type of user is applying for the new service, for example, known user or new. Console display name: "".
* `yearOfBirth` (string): A user's birth year. It is mandatory for IP activities and recommended FP activities. Console display name: "".
* `yob` (string): A user's age range. Console display name: "".

```terraform
  environment_id = var.pingone_environment_id

  connector = {
    id = "biocatchConnector"
  }
```

## CLEAR

Connector ID (`connector.id` in the resource): `connectorClear`

Properties (used under the `properties` block in the resource as a key in the JSON object):

* `authType` (string): Console display name: "".
* `button` (string): Console display name: "Verify with CLEAR".
* `customAuth` (string): Console display name: "".
* `customFields` (string): Custom key-value pairs passed to CLEAR (e.g., your internal customer or employee ID for identity matching). Console display name: "Custom Fields".
* `showPoweredBy` (string): Console display name: "".
* `skipButtonPress` (string): Console display name: "".
* `url` (string): The target URL for the post-verification redirect. Console display name: "Redirect URL".
* `userId` (string): CLEAR user ID for reverification. When provided, triggers a reverification flow against an existing CLEAR identity instead of a full initial verification. Console display name: "User ID".
* `userProfileAddressCity` (string): User's city for CLEAR identity matching. Console display name: "City".
* `userProfileAddressCountry` (string): User's country for CLEAR identity matching. Console display name: "Country".
* `userProfileAddressLine1` (string): User's street address line 1 for CLEAR identity matching. Console display name: "Address Line 1".
* `userProfileAddressLine2` (string): User's street address line 2 for CLEAR identity matching. Console display name: "Address Line 2".
* `userProfileAddressPostalCode` (string): User's postal code for CLEAR identity matching. Console display name: "Postal Code".
* `userProfileAddressState` (string): User's state for CLEAR identity matching. Console display name: "State".
* `userProfileDob` (string): User's date of birth for CLEAR identity matching. Console display name: "Date of Birth".
* `userProfileEmail` (string): User's email address for CLEAR identity matching. Console display name: "Email".
* `userProfileFirstName` (string): User's first name for CLEAR identity matching. Console display name: "First Name".
* `userProfileLastName` (string): User's last name for CLEAR identity matching. Console display name: "Last Name".
* `userProfilePhone` (string): User's phone number for CLEAR identity matching. Console display name: "Phone".

## Challenge

Connector ID (`connector.id` in the resource): `challengeConnector`

Properties (used under the `properties` block in the resource as a key in the JSON object):

* `challenge` (string): Console display name: "Challenge".
* `challengeStatus` (string): started:
This status signifies that the challenge has been created and can be polled until the status changes or times out

approved:
This status signifies that the challenge has been approved and should be treated as a success event

denied:
This status signifies that the challenge has been denied. This status will still be treated as a success event and the flow is expected to move forward to the true path. Flow can then decide what next to do with the denied status. Console display name: "".

## Credova

Connector ID (`connector.id` in the resource): `credovaConnector`

Properties (used under the `properties` block in the resource as a key in the JSON object):

* `bankAccountInstitutionName` (string): Name of the Bank where User has an account. Console display name: "Bank Name".
* `bankAccountNameOnAccount` (string): User's name present on the Bank Account. Console display name: "Name on Bank Account".
* `bankAccountNumber` (string): Account Number of User's Bank Account. Console display name: "Bank Account Number".
* `bankAccountRoutingNumber` (string): Routing Number of User's Bank Account. Console display name: "Bank Account Routing Number".
* `bankAccountType` (string): Type of Bank Account the User has: SAVING/CHECKING. Console display name: "Bank Account Type".
* `baseUrl` (string): Base URL for Credova API. Console display name: "Base URL".
* `city` (string): City of the User. Console display name: "City".
* `dateOfBirth` (string): Birthday of the User in the format: dd-mm-yyyy. Console display name: "Birth Date".
* `email` (string): Email address of the User. Console display name: "Email Address".
* `firstName` (string): First Name of the User. Console display name: "First Name".
* `lastName` (string): Last Name of the User. Console display name: "Last Name".
* `middleInitial` (string): Middle Initial of the User. Console display name: "Middle Initial".
* `mobilePhone` (string): Phone Number of the User in the format: 123-456-7890. Console display name: "Mobile Number".
* `offerId` (string): Console display name: "Offer ID".
* `password` (string): Password for the Credova Developer Portal. Console display name: "Credova Password".
* `publicId` (string): Console display name: "Public ID".
* `ssn` (string): Social Security Number of the User. You can use full or last 4 digit of SSN. Console display name: "SSN".
* `state` (string): State of the User. Console display name: "State".
* `storeCode` (string): Store Code of the Company provided by Credova. Console display name: "Store Code".
* `street` (string): Street Address of the User. Console display name: "Street Address".
* `suiteApartment` (string): Apartment Number of the User. Console display name: "Apartment".
* `username` (string): Username for the Credova Developer Portal. Console display name: "Credova Username".
* `zipCode` (string): Zip Code of the User. Console display name: "ZIP Code".

## CrowdStrike

Connector ID (`connector.id` in the resource): `crowdStrikeConnector`

Properties (used under the `properties` block in the resource as a key in the JSON object):

* `alertLimit` (string): The maximum number of CrowdStrike alerts to return for the device. Default is 100. Console display name: "Alert Limit".
* `baseURL` (string): The base URL of the CrowdStrike environment. Console display name: "CrowdStrike Base URL".
* `clientId` (string): The Client ID of the application in CrowdStrike. Console display name: "Client ID".
* `clientSecret` (string): The Client Secret provided by CrowdStrike. Console display name: "Client Secret".
* `deviceIdAlertRisk` (string): The CrowdStrike device ID (also known as agent ID), such as “f69915c8a8b244a1a7c4e4a4d7870e2f”. Console display name: "Device ID".
* `deviceIdDeviceManaged` (string): The CrowdStrike device ID (also known as agent ID), such as “f69915c8a8b244a1a7c4e4a4d7870e2f”. Console display name: "Device ID".
* `deviceIds` (string): List of Device IDs (JSON Array formatted). Console display name: "Device IDs".
* `domainForAnalysis` (string): Target domain for risk analysis. Console display name: "Domain".
* `email` (string): The email of the user associated with the device. Console display name: "Email".
* `filter` (string): Optional filter and sort criteria in the form of an FQL query. Console display name: "Filter".
* `ip` (string): The user's IP address. Console display name: "IP".
* `lastSeenDays` (string): The number of days to search back in time for a managed device. Console display name: "Last Seen Number of Days".
* `limit` (string): The maximum records to return. [1-500]. Console display name: "Limit".
* `offset` (string): Starting index of overall result set from which to return ids. Console display name: "Offset".
* `searchLoginDays` (string): The number of days to search back in time for a login. Console display name: "Search Back Number of Days".
* `username` (string): The username associated with the device. Console display name: "Username".
* `usernameForAnalysis` (string): Target username for risk analysis. Console display name: "Username".

## Daon IdentityX

Connector ID (`connector.id` in the resource): `daonConnector`

Properties (used under the `properties` block in the resource as a key in the JSON object):

* `apiUrl` (string): The protocol, host and base path to the IdX API. E.g. https://api.identityx-cloud.com/tenant1/IdentityXServices/rest/v1. Console display name: "API Base URL".
* `authId` (string): The identifier of the authentication request to be retrieved. Console display name: "Authentication Request Id".
* `description` (string): A description of the authentication request - if using the IdentityX Authenticator, this will be provided to the user. Console display name: "Authentication Description".
* `password` (string): The password of the user to authenticate API calls. Console display name: "Admin Password".
* `policyUrl` (string): The policy associated with the authentication request. Console display name: "Policy URL".
* `pushNotificationType` (string): Provides operation instructions to the mobile application how to behave when a push notification is received. Console display name: "Push Notification Type".
* `secureImageTransactionContent` (string): Image to be displayed securely to a user. The secureTransactionContentType property must be "image/png" or "text/plain;image/png". Console display name: "Secure Image Transaction Content".
* `secureTextTransactionContent` (string): Text to be displayed securely to a user. The secureTransactionContentType property must be "text/plain" or "text/plain;image/png". Console display name: "Secure Text Transaction Content".
* `secureTransactionContentType` (string): Describes the value of the secureTransactionContent and secureTextTransactionContent property. Console display name: "Secure Transaction Content Type".
* `type` (string): Specifies the protocol type of the authentication request. Console display name: "Authentication Type".
* `userId` (string): The ID of the user. Console display name: "User ID".
* `userLogin` (string): The userId of the user you want to retrieve. E.g. user@example.com. Console display name: "User Login".
* `username` (string): The userId to authenticate API calls. Console display name: "Admin Username".


Example:
```terraform
resource "pingone_davinci_connector_instance" "daonConnector" {
  environment_id = var.pingone_environment_id

  connector = {
    id = "daonConnector"
  }
  name = "My awesome daonConnector"
  property {
    name  = "apiUrl"
    type  = "string"
    value = var.daonconnector_property_api_url
  }
  property {
    name  = "authId"
    type  = "string"
    value = var.daonconnector_property_auth_id
  }
  property {
    name  = "description"
    type  = "string"
    value = var.daonconnector_property_description
  }
  property {
    name  = "password"
    type  = "string"
    value = var.daonconnector_property_password
  }
  property {
    name  = "policyUrl"
    type  = "string"
    value = var.daonconnector_property_policy_url
  }
  property {
    name  = "pushNotificationType"
    type  = "string"
    value = var.daonconnector_property_push_notification_type
  }
  property {
    name  = "secureImageTransactionContent"
    type  = "string"
    value = var.daonconnector_property_secure_image_transaction_content
  }
  property {
    name  = "secureTextTransactionContent"
    type  = "string"
    value = var.daonconnector_property_secure_text_transaction_content
  }
  property {
    name  = "secureTransactionContentType"
    type  = "string"
    value = var.daonconnector_property_secure_transaction_content_type
  }
  property {
    name  = "type"
    type  = "string"
    value = var.daonconnector_property_type
  }
  property {
    name  = "userId"
```

* `apiV1MonitorGet_id_offset` (string): Use this parameter for paginating through large sets of monitors. Start with a value of zero, make a request, set the value to the last ID of result set, and then repeat until the response is empty. Console display name: "Id_offset".
* `apiV1MonitorGet_monitor_tags` (string): A comma separated list indicating what service and/or custom tags, if any, should be used to filter the list of monitors. Tags created in the Datadog UI automatically have the service key prepended. For example, `service:my-app`. Console display name: "Monitor_tags".
* `apiV1MonitorGet_name` (string): A string to filter monitors by name. Console display name: "Name".
* `apiV1MonitorGet_page` (string): The page to start paginating from. If this argument is not specified, the request returns all monitors without pagination. Console display name: "Page".
* `apiV1MonitorGet_page_size` (string): The number of monitors to return per page. If the page argument is not specified, the default behavior returns all monitors without a `page_size` limit. However, if page is specified and `page_size` is not, the argument defaults to 100. Console display name: "Page_size".
* `apiV1MonitorGet_tags` (string): A comma separated list indicating what tags, if any, should be used to filter the list of monitors by scope. For example, `host:host0`. Console display name: "Tags".
* `apiV1MonitorGet_with_downtimes` (string): If this argument is set to true, then the returned data includes all current active downtimes for each monitor. Console display name: "With_downtimes".

## DeBounce

Connector ID (`connector.id` in the resource): `connectorDeBounce`

Properties (used under the `properties` block in the resource as a key in the JSON object):

* `apiKey` (string): A DeBounce API Key is physically a token/code of 13 random alphanumeric characters. If you need to create an API key, please log in to your DeBounce account and then navigate to the API section. Console display name: "API Key".
* `append` (string): To find full name and avatar of an email owner set to “true”. (Turn toggle switch on). Console display name: "Append".
* `email` (string): Email address you are validating. Also used for using the free DeBounce API, Disposable Email Detector. Console display name: "Email".
* `endDate` (string): End Date in format “YY-MM-DD”. Console display name: "End Date".
* `gsuite` (string): If you require to detect the validity of G Suite Accept-all emails, set it true. (Turn toggle switch on). Console display name: "Gsuite".
* `listID` (string): When checking status of a bulk upload: ID of the list you have uploaded using bulk validation API. Console display name: "List ID".
* `listURL` (string): When performing bulk validation, this is the URL of your .csv or .txt email list. Console display name: "URL for email list".
* `photo` (string): If require profile photo along with the validation results set to “true”. (Turn toggle switch on). Console display name: "Photo".
* `startDate` (string): Start Date in format “YY-MM-DD”. Console display name: "Start Date".


Example:
```terraform
resource "pingone_davinci_connector_instance" "connectorDeBounce" {
  environment_id = var.pingone_environment_id

  connector = {
    id = "connectorDeBounce"
  }
  name = "My awesome connectorDeBounce"
  property {
    name  = "apiKey"
    type  = "string"
    value = var.connectordebounce_property_api_key
  }
  property {
    name  = "append"
    type  = "string"
    value = var.connectordebounce_property_append
  }
  property {
    name  = "email"
    type  = "string"
    value = var.connectordebounce_property_email
  }
  property {
    name  = "endDate"
    type  = "string"
    value = var.connectordebounce_property_end_date
  }
  property {
    name  = "gsuite"
    type  = "string"
    value = var.connectordebounce_property_gsuite
  }
  property {
    name  = "listID"
    type  = "string"
    value = var.connectordebounce_property_list_id
  }
  property {
    name  = "listURL"
    type  = "string"
    value = var.connectordebounce_property_list_url
  }
  property {
    name  = "photo"
    type  = "string"
    value = var.connectordebounce_property_photo
  }
  property {
    name  = "startDate"
    type  = "string"
    value = var.connectordebounce_property_start_date
  }
}
```

## Druva inSync Cloud API

Connector ID (`connector.id` in the resource): `connector-oai-druvainsynccloud`

Properties (used under the `properties` block in the resource as a key in the JSON object):

* `authClientId` (string): The Client ID of the authenticating application. Console display name: "Client ID".
* `authClientSecret` (string): The Secret Key for the authenticating application. Console display name: "Secret Key".
* `authTokenUrl` (string): The URL used to obtain an access token. Console display name: "Token URL".
* `basePath` (string): The base URL for contacting the API. Console display name: "Base Path".
* `clientsGet_connection_status` (string): The connection status of the client. It can be 'Connected', 'Disconnected', or 'Not Registered'. Console display name: "ConnectionStatus".
* `clientsGet_page_number` (string): Search by Page Number. Example - 1. Console display name: "PageNumber".
* `clientsGet_page_size` (string): Search by Page Size. Example - 100. Console display name: "PageSize".
* `clientsGet_search_by` (string): Search by the name of the eDiscovery Download Client. Example - Client1. Console display name: "SearchBy".
* `clientsGet_sort_by` (string): Key to sort the results. You can sort by: name/clientVersion/cplatform/createdBy. Console display name: "SortBy".
* `clientsGet_sort_order` (string): Specify the parameter by which you intend to sort the listed results. Sorting can be done in ascending or descending order. Console display name: "SortOrder".
* `createNewJob_createDownloadJobRequest_CreateDownloadJobRequest_clientName` (string): Name of the eDiscovery Download Client. Example - Client1. Console display name: "ClientName".
* `createNewJob_createDownloadJobRequest_CreateDownloadJobRequest_createdBy` (string): Name of administrator triggering the job. Example - Ernie Carter. Console display name: "CreatedBy".
* `createNewJob_createDownloadJobRequest_CreateDownloadJobRequest_custodianEmails` (string): Console display name: "CustodianEmails".
* `createNewJob_createDownloadJobRequest_CreateDownloadJobRequest_downloadLocation` (string): Location to download the job. Example - D:\Downloads. Console display name: "DownloadLocation".
* `createNewJob_createDownloadJobRequest_CreateDownloadJobRequest_downloadOption` (string): 0 indicates only metadata, 1 indicates data and metadata and 2 indicates zip download option. Console display name: "DownloadOption".
* `createNewJob_createDownloadJobRequest_CreateDownloadJobRequest_enable_data_integrity` (string): Use &#39;true&#39; to enable data integrity and &#39;false&#39; to disable data integrity. Console display name: "Enable_data_integrity".
* `createNewJob_createDownloadJobRequest_CreateDownloadJobRequest_legalholdId` (string): Legal Hold ID for which download is to be triggered. Example -10. Console display name: "LegalholdId".
* `endpointsV1BackupsGet_device_id` (string): Filter to get list of last successful backups for a particular device using its unique ID. Get the ID of a device using the ‘List all devices’ API.  Console display name: "DeviceID".
* `endpointsV1BackupsGet_last_successful` (string): Provides details of the last successful backup for a device.  Currently, only 'True' is the supported value for this parameter. Console display name: "LastSuccessful".
* `endpointsV1BackupsGet_max_backup_end_time` (string): Filter to list successful backups that ended before a particular date and time. Format - YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ. Console display name: "MaxBackupEndTime".
* `endpointsV1BackupsGet_max_backup_start_time` (string): Filter to list successful backups that started before a particular date and time. Format - YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ. Console display name: "MaxBackupStartTime".
* `endpointsV1BackupsGet_min_backup_end_time` (string): Filter to list successful backups that ended after a particular date and time. Format - YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ. Console display name: "MinBackupEndTime".
* `endpointsV1BackupsGet_min_backup_start_time` (string): Filter to list successful backups that started after a particular date and time. Format - YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ. Console display name: "MinBackupStartTime".
* `endpointsV1BackupsGet_page_token` (string): The token to access the next page of results. Use the token value received in the previous response's parameter 'nextPageToken'. Console display name: "PageToken".
* `endpointsV1BackupsGet_user_id` (string): Filter to get list of last successful backups on devices owned by a particular user using their user ID. Get the ID of a user using the ‘List all users’ API. Console display name: "UserID".
* `endpointsV1DevicemappingsGet_device_identifier` (string): Specify the unique id of the device for the selected deviceIdentifierType in inSync. Console display name: "DeviceIdentifier".
* `endpointsV1DevicemappingsGet_device_identifier_type` (string): Filter to list device mappings using the unique device identifier type of the device.(serial-number, uuid, or hostname). Console display name: "DeviceIdentifierType".
* `endpointsV1DevicemappingsGet_email_id` (string): Filter to list device mappings using the email address of a user. Console display name: "EmailID".
* `endpointsV1DevicemappingsGet_restore_data` (string): Filter to list device mappings using the type of data restore performed. Console display name: "RestoreData".
* `endpointsV1DevicemappingsMappingIDDelete_mapping_id` (string): The id associated with the device mapping. Get the mapping id by running the List Device Mapping API. Console display name: "MappingID".
* `endpointsV1DevicemappingsPost_endpointsV1DevicemappingsGetRequest_EndpointsV1DevicemappingsGetRequest_deviceIdentifier` (string): Specify the unique device identifier for the selected type. (serial-number, uuid, or hostname). Console display name: "DeviceIdentifier".
* `endpointsV1DevicemappingsPost_endpointsV1DevicemappingsGetRequest_EndpointsV1DevicemappingsGetRequest_deviceIdentifierType` (string): Specify the unique device identifier type of the device.(serial-number, uuid, or hostname). Console display name: "DeviceIdentifierType".
* `endpointsV1DevicemappingsPost_endpointsV1DevicemappingsGetRequest_EndpointsV1DevicemappingsGetRequest_deviceName` (string): Specify the name of the device that is registered with the user. Example - Ernie Carter&#39;s Macbook. Console display name: "DeviceName".
* `endpointsV1DevicemappingsPost_endpointsV1DevicemappingsGetRequest_EndpointsV1DevicemappingsGetRequest_emailID` (string): Specify the email address of the user. Example - ernie.carter@druva.com. Console display name: "EmailID".
* `endpointsV1DevicemappingsPost_endpointsV1DevicemappingsGetRequest_EndpointsV1DevicemappingsGetRequest_oldDeviceName` (string): Name of the user&#39;s old device in Druva inSync that is to be replaced with a new device.   :fa-info-circle: Note: Specify the value for this parameter only if you want to replace the device for the user, else keep this field blank. Console display name: "OldDeviceName".
* `endpointsV1DevicemappingsPost_endpointsV1DevicemappingsGetRequest_EndpointsV1DevicemappingsGetRequest_restoreData` (string): The type of data restore to be performed.(ALL, SYSTEM, OR DATA)  Type of data to be restored on the new device.Specify one of the following value:  1) All - To restore both, the data and the system settings from the existing device on the new device. 2) SYSTEM - To restore only the system settings from the existing device on the new device. 3)DATA - To restore only the data from the existing device on the new device.  :fa-info-circle: Note: Specify the value for this parameter only if you want to replace the device for the user, else keep this field blank. Console display name: "RestoreData".

If there are more than 500 events, the response also contains a Tracker, an identifier that contains inSync database reference and identifies the next set of unique events when a successive Events API call is made. Do not include the Tracker in the first Events API request. :fa-info-circle:If you do not specify the Tracker in the successive request, inSync returns you the same list of events in response that you received in the first Event API request. The new profile settings are applied to the user account in the next backup cycle.Get the profile ID using the &#39;List all profiles&#39; API.  :fa-info-circle: If you are changing user&#39;s profile to a profile where the Privacy Settings conflicts with the Privacy Settings in the old profile, which may result in administrators getting an unintentional access to the user&#39;s data, inSync does not allow you to update the profile. In such a case, you must request the inSync user to allow the inSync administrators to access their backed up data (setting on inSync Client) and try again. Console display name: "ProfileID".
* `usermanagementV1UsersUserIDPatch_usermanagementV1UsersUserIDDeleteRequest1_UsermanagementV1UsersUserIDDeleteRequest1_storageID` (string): Specify the ID of the new storage that you want to associate with the user account.Get the storage ID using the &#39;List all storages&#39; API.  After you change the user&#39;s storage:  1)User data is backed up to the new storage.  2)Snapshots on the old storage are retained and compacted following the retention policy.  3) User can restore data from snapshots saved on old as well as the new storage. Console display name: "StorageID".
* `usermanagementV1UsersUserIDPatch_usermanagementV1UsersUserIDDeleteRequest1_UsermanagementV1UsersUserIDDeleteRequest1_userName` (string): Specify the new username for the user. Console display name: "UserName".
* `usermanagementV1UsersUserIDPreservePost_user_id` (string): The unique ID of a user in inSync. Get the ID of a user using the 'List all users' API. Console display name: "UserID".
* `usermanagementV1UsersUserIDResetPasswordPost_user_id` (string): The unique ID of a user in inSync. Get the ID of a user using the 'List all users' API. Console display name: "UserID".

## Duo

Connector ID (`connector.id` in the resource): `duoConnector`

Properties (used under the `properties` block in the resource as a key in the JSON object):

* `authType` (string): Console display name: "".
* `button` (string): Console display name: "Duo MFA".
* `customAuth` (string): Console display name: "".
* `showPoweredBy` (string): Console display name: "".
* `skipButtonPress` (string): Console display name: "".
* `username` (string): Console display name: "Username".


Example:
```terraform
resource "pingone_davinci_connector_instance" "duoConnector" {
  environment_id = var.pingone_environment_id

  connector = {
    id = "duoConnector"
  }
  name = "My awesome duoConnector"
  property {
    name  = "authType"
    type  = "string"
    value = var.duoconnector_property_auth_type
  }
  property {
    name  = "button"
    type  = "string"
    value = var.duoconnector_property_button
  }
  property {
    name  = "customAuth"
    type  = "string"
    value = jsonencode({})
  }
  property {
    name  = "showPoweredBy"
    type  = "string"
    value = var.duoconnector_property_show_powered_by
  }
  property {
    name  = "skipButtonPress"
    type  = "string"
    value = var.duoconnector_property_skip_button_press
  }
  property {
    name  = "username"
    type  = "string"
    value = var.duoconnector_property_username
  }
}
```


## Entrust

Connector ID (`connector.id` in the resource): `entrustConnector`

Properties (used under the `properties` block in the resource as a key in the JSON object):

* `applicationId` (string): The application ID for the Identity as a Service application. Console display name: "Application ID".
* `htmlConfig0` (string): Console display name: "".
* `htmlConfig1` (string): Console display name: "".
* `htmlConfig2` (string): Console display name: "".
* `serviceDomain` (string): The domain of the Entrust service. Format is '<customer>.<region>.trustedauth.com'. For example, 'mycompany.us.trustedauth.com'. Console display name: "Service Domain".
* `transactionDetails` (string): Additional transaction details to send to Entrust. Console display name: "Transaction Details".
* `userId` (string): The unique ID of the user you want to authenticate. Console display name: "User ID".


Example:
```terraform
resource "pingone_davinci_connector_instance" "entrustConnector" {
  environment_id = var.pingone_environment_id

  connector = {
    id = "entrustConnector"
  }
  name = "My awesome entrustConnector"
  property {
    name  = "applicationId"
    type  = "string"
    value = var.entrustconnector_property_application_id
  }
  property {
    name  = "htmlConfig0"
    type  = "string"
    value = var.entrustconnector_property_html_config0
  }
  property {
    name  = "htmlConfig1"
    type  = "string"
    value = var.entrustconnector_property_html_config1
  }
  property {
    name  = "htmlConfig2"
    type  = "string"
    value = var.entrustconnector_property_html_config2
  }
  property {
    name  = "serviceDomain"
    type  = "string"
    value = var.entrustconnector_property_service_domain
  }
  property {
    name  = "transactionDetails"
    type  = "string"
    value = var.entrustconnector_property_transaction_details
  }
  property {
    name  = "userId"
    type  = "string"
    value = var.entrustconnector_property_user_id
  }
}
```


## Equifax

Connector ID (`connector.id` in the resource): `equifaxConnector`

Properties (used under the `properties` block in the resource as a key in the JSON object):

* `accountNumber` (string): The account number can be a credit card, auto loan, HELOC, a mortgage account number, CHKACCT or SAVACCT (Demand Deposit Accounts). Console display name: "Account Number".
* `accountType` (string): Console display name: "".
* `addressLine1` (string): First line of address. Console display name: "Address Line 1".
* `addressLine2` (string): Second line of address. Console display name: "Address Line 2".
* `baseUrl` (string): Base URL for Equifax API. Console display name: "Base URL".
* `cid` (string): This is CID which uniquely identifies PII. This Key is generated by Equifax Internal Systems. Console display name: "CID which uniquely identifies PII".
* `city` (string): City of the Consumer. Console display name: "City".
* `clientId` (string): When you Create a New App, Equifax will assign a Client ID per environment for the API Product. Console display name: "Client ID".
* `clientSecret` (string): When you Create a New App, Equifax will assign a Client Secret per environment for the API Product. Console display name: "Client Secret".
* `cnx` (string): This is ConnexusKey which uniquely identifies PII. This Key is generated by Equifax Internal Systems. Console display name: "ConnexusKey".
* `currentAddressLine` (string): Current address. Console display name: "Current Address Line".
* `currentCity` (string): City of the Current Address. Console display name: "Current Address City".
* `currentState` (string): State of the Current Address Abbreviation (eg: AZ, FL, NY). Console display name: "Current Address State".
* `currentZip` (string): Zip code of the Current Address. Console display name: "Current Address ZIP".
* `customerId` (string): Unique identifier of the consumer, this could be transaction id or any type of identifier that is associated with the consumer, account, etc. Console display name: "Customer ID".
* `deliveryChannel` (string): Identifier for product API to identify the delivery channel. Please contact Equifax Sales Representative during client onboarding for this value. Console display name: "Delivery Channel".
* `dob` (string): Consumer's Date of Birth (YYYYMMDD). Console display name: "Date of Birth".
* `dobDay` (string): Day of the consumer’s birth. Allowed values (0-31). Console display name: "Birth Day".
* `dobMonth` (string): Month of the consumer’s birth. Allowed values (01-12). Console display name: "Birth Month".
* `dobYear` (string): Year of the consumer’s birth. Console display name: "Birth Year".
* `driversLicenseNumber` (string): Consumer’s Drivers License Number. Console display name: "Drivers License Number".
* `driversLicenseState` (string): Issuing state of driver’s license abbreviation (eg: AZ, FL, NY). Console display name: "Drivers License State".
* `efxClientCorrelationId` (string): ID provided by client to uniquely track service request. Console display name: "Client Correlation ID".
* `email` (string): Consumer's Email address. Console display name: "Email".
* `equifaxQuery` (string): Console display name: "".
* `equifaxSoapApiEnvironment` (string): Console display name: "".
* `firstName` (string): Consumer's First Name. Console display name: "First Name".
* `formerAddressLine` (string): Former Address. Console display name: "Former Address Line".
* `formerCity` (string): City of the Former Address. Console display name: "Former Address City".
* `formerState` (string): State of the Former Address Abbreviation (eg: AZ, FL, NY). Console display name: "Former Address State".
* `formerZip` (string): Zip code of the Former Address. Console display name: "Former Address ZIP".
* `hitCode` (string): Console display name: "".
* `lastName` (string): Consumer's Last Name. Console display name: "Last Name".
* `memberNumber` (string): Unique Identifier of Customer. Please contact Equifax Sales Representative during client onboarding for this value. Console display name: "Member Number".
* `middleInitial` (string): Consumer's Middle Initial. Console display name: "Middle Initial".
* `middleName` (string): Consumer's Middle Name. Console display name: "Middle Name".
* `nameSuffix` (string): Consumer's Suffix. Valid Values: "JR", "SR", "I", "II", "III", "IV", "V", "VI", "VII","VIII" or "IX". Console display name: "Name Suffix".
* `orchestrationCode` (string): OrchestrationCode in the request represents data flow across all functions provided by the Identity Service. Based on a use case, the Orchestration Code sent in the request processes the service / product flows and provides results of one or many pre-configured requested orchestration policies. Console display name: "Orchestration Code".
* `password` (string): Password provided by Equifax for SOAP API. Console display name: "Password for SOAP API".
* `phoneNumber` (string): Consumer's Phone number, the format should contain only numbers. Console display name: "Phone Number".
* `ssn` (string): Consumer's Social Security Number in XXXXXXXXX or XXXX format. Console display name: "Social Security Number".
* `state` (string): State of the Consumer Abbreviation (eg: AZ, FL, NY). Console display name: "State".
* `synthetic2RulesCategory` (string): Console display name: "".
* `transactionTimestamp` (string): Timestamp to start search from, epoch time in milliseconds. Console display name: "Transaction Timestamp".
* `username` (string): Username provided by Equifax for SOAP API. Console display name: "Username for SOAP API".
* `zip` (string): Zip code of the Consumer. Console display name: "ZIP".

```terraform
          "preferredControlType" : "textField",
          "disabled" : true,
          "initializeValue" : "SINGULARKEY_REDIRECT_URI",
          "copyToClip" : true
        },
        "clientId" : {
          "type" : "string",
          "displayName" : "Application ID",
          "preferredControlType" : "textField",
          "required" : true,
          "value" : "${var.facebookidpconnector_property_application_id}"
        },
        "clientSecret" : {
          "type" : "string",
          "displayName" : "Client Secret",
          "preferredControlType" : "textField",
          "secure" : true,
          "required" : true,
          "value" : "${var.facebookidpconnector_property_client_secret}"
        },
        "scope" : {
          "type" : "string",
          "displayName" : "Scope",
          "preferredControlType" : "textField",
          "requiredValue" : "email",
          "required" : true,
          "value" : "${var.facebookidpconnector_property_scope}"
        },
        "disableCreateUser" : {
          "displayName" : "Disable Shadow User",
          "preferredControlType" : "toggleSwitch",
          "value" : true,
          "info" : "A shadow user is implicitly created, unless disabled."
        },
        "userConnectorAttributeMapping" : {
          "type" : "object",
          "displayName" : null,
          "preferredControlType" : "userConnectorAttributeMapping",
          "newMappingAllowed" : true,
          "title1" : null,
          "title2" : null,
          "sections" : [
            "attributeMapping"
          ],
          "value" : {
            "userPoolConnectionId" : "defaultUserPool",
            "mapping" : {
              "username" : {
                "value1" : "id"
              },
              "name" : {
                "value1" : "name"
              },
              "email" : {
                "value1" : "email"
              }
            }
          }
        },
        "customAttributes" : {
          "type" : "array",
          "displayName" : "Connector Attributes",
          "preferredControlType" : "tableViewAttributes",
          "info" : "These attributes will be available in User Connector Attribute Mapping.",
          "sections" : [
            "connectorAttributes"
          ],
          "value" : [
            {
              "name" : "id",
              "description" : "ID",
              "type" : "string",
              "value" : null,
              "minLength" : "1",
              "maxLength" : "300",
              "required" : true,
              "attributeType" : "sk"
            },
            {
              "name" : "name",
              "description" : "Display Name",
              "type" : "string",
              "value" : null,
              "minLength" : "1",
              "maxLength" : "250",
              "required" : false,
              "attributeType" : "sk"
            },
            {
              "name" : "email",
              "description" : "Email",
              "type" : "string",
              "value" : null,
              "minLength" : "1",
              "maxLength" : "250",
              "required" : false,
              "attributeType" : "sk"
            }
          ]
        },
        "state" : {
          "displayName" : "Send state with request",
          "value" : true,
          "preferredControlType" : "toggleSwitch",
          "info" : "Send unique state value with every request"
        },
        "returnToUrl" : {
          "displayName" : "Application Return To URL",
          "preferredControlType" : "textField",
          "info" : "When using the embedded flow player widget and an IDP/Social Login connector, provide a callback URL to return back to the application.",
          "value" : "${var.facebookidpconnector_property_callback_url}"
        }
      }
    })
  }
  property {
    name  = "showPoweredBy"
    type  = "string"
    value = var.facebookidpconnector_property_show_powered_by
  }
  property {
    name  = "skipButtonPress"
    type  = "string"
    value = var.facebookidpconnector_property_skip_button_press
  }
}
```

## Finicity

Connector ID (`connector.id` in the resource): `finicityConnector`

Properties (used under the `properties` block in the resource as a key in the JSON object):

* `address` (string): Address of the User. Console display name: "Address".
* `appKey` (string): Finicity App Key from Finicity Developer Portal. Console display name: "Finicity App Key".
* `baseUrl` (string): Base URL for Finicity API. Console display name: "Base URL".
* `city` (string): City of the User. Console display name: "City".
* `dayOfMonth` (string): The birthday 2-digit day-of-month. Console display name: "Birth Day".
* `finicityConnectType` (string): The type of connect flow you want for the customer/consumer. See Finicity Connect Type For Definitions. Console display name: "Finicity Connect Type".
* `finicityCustomerType` (string): Console display name: "Finicity Customer Type".
* `firstName` (string): First Name of the User. Console display name: "First Name".
* `fromDate` (string): The fromDate parameter is an Epoch Timestamp (in seconds), such as 1494449017. If included, the epoch timestamp should be 10 digits long and be within the Report's limit. Console display name: "From Date".
* `lastName` (string): Last Name of the User. Console display name: "Last Name".
* `mainHeaderText` (string): Console display name: "".
* `month` (string): The birthday 2-digit month (01 is January). Console display name: "Birth Month".
* `nextButtonText` (string): Console display name: "".
* `partnerId` (string): The partner id you can obtain from your Finicity developer dashboard. Console display name: "Partner ID".
* `partnerSecret` (string): Partner Secret from Finicity Developer Portal. Console display name: "Partner Secret".
* `phone` (string): Phone Number of the User. Console display name: "Phone Number".
* `screen0Config` (string): Console display name: "".
* `screen1Config` (string): Console display name: "".
* `ssn` (string): SSN of the User. Console display name: "Social Security Number".
* `state` (string): State of the User. Console display name: "State".
* `title` (string): Console display name: "".
* `year` (string): The birthday 4-digit year. Console display name: "Birth Year".
* `zip` (string): Zip code of the User. Console display name: "ZIP".

## Form

Connector ID (`connector.id` in the resource): `pingOneFormsConnector`

Properties (used under the `properties` block in the resource as a key in the JSON object):

* `agreement` (string): The agreement to show to the user. For a dynamic agreement, select Use Agreement ID and enter a value in the Agreement ID field. Console display name: "Agreement".
* `agreementId` (string): Enter the ID of the agreement to show, such as "68373acc-c0ef-4258-b69d-8152320a8237". This allows you to show a different agreement depending on the flow context. Console display name: "Agreement ID".
* `agreementSectionLabel` (string): Console display name: "Agreement".
* `authenticationMethodList` (string): The list of MFA authentication methods that you want to make available to the user, such as "EMAIL,TOTP". To allow all devices, enter "EMAIL, MOBILE, SMS, VOICE, TOTP, FIDO2, MAGIC_LINK, YUBIKEY, OATH_TOKEN, WHATSAPP, PINGID_DESKTOP_GEN2". Separate multiple values with a comma. Console display name: "Custom Authentication Method List".
* `authenticationMethodSource` (string): Determines where to get the list of authentication methods to present to the user. Select an MFA policy, specify a policy ID, or specify the exact authentication method list. If the selected policy is no longer available at runtime, the default MFA policy is used. Console display name: "Authentication Method Source".
* `buttonText` (string): The text to show on the continue button, such as "Submit" or "Continue". Console display name: "Button Text".
* `challenge` (string): Select a challenge variable from your flow, such as from a Challenge or Flow Conductor node. When this challenge is completed in another branch of the flow, the main flow continues past the form. Console display name: "".
* `collectBehavioralData` (string): When enabled, collects behavioral data to identify non-human activity. Enable Device Profiling must be enabled beforehand. Console display name: "Include Behavioral Data".
* `componentVisibility` (string): For form components with a visibility setting of "Show by default" or "Hide by default", this table allows you to override the default visibility. Provide a value of "true" to show a component, or provide a value of "false" to hide a component. If no boolean is provided, each component follows its own visibility setting. Visibility keys are defined in your form. You can override the visibility of multiple form components with one boolean value by setting the same visibility key for all of the components. Console display name: "Component Visibility".
* `deviceProfilingSectionLabel` (string): Console display name: "Device Profiling".
* `dynamicText` (string): Provide a string to populate the dynamic text in your form. Dynamic text is defined in Translatable Rich Text and Label fields by wrapping a key in curly braces, such as {{userFirstName}}. Console display name: "Dynamic Text".
* `enableMagicLinkAuthentication` (string): When enabled, the Magic Link option is available in the authentication method list. Console display name: "Enable Magic Link Authentication".
* `enablePolling` (string): Use polling to loop this part of the flow, or a challenge to pause the flow on this node, while waiting for another part of the flow to complete. Console display name: "Enable Polling".
* `enableRisk` (string): Enable PingOne Protect SDK to collect device information. Console display name: "Enable Device Profiling".
* `form` (string): The form to show. You can add forms in PingOne > User Experience > Forms. Console display name: "Form".
* `formData` (string): Optionally provide a value to pre-populate the fields in your form. Users can keep the pre-populated value or change it before submitting the form. Console display name: "Initial Field Values".
* `hyperlinkUrls` (string): The URL for the image hyperlink, such as "https://example.com/sign-up". Console display name: "Hyperlink URLs".
* `imageSectionLabel` (string): Console display name: "Image".
* `imageUrls` (string): The URL for the image to show, such as "https://example.com/image.jpg". Console display name: "Image URLs".
* `innerCss` (string): Console display name: "CSS".
* `innerHtml` (string): Console display name: "Inner HTML".
* `isIAFDetectionEnabled` (string): Identify the agent used to access the application and detect if it is an IAF (Intelligent Automation Framework) agent. Console display name: "Enable IAF Detection (Experimental)".
* `linkBrandingThemesUrl` (string): Console display name: "Branding and Themes".
* `linkFormsUrl` (string): Console display name: "Forms".
* `linkMFAPolicies` (string): Console display name: "MFA Policies".
* `linkWithP1User` (string): When enabled, DaVinci creates or updates a linked PingOne user account using attributes from the external IdP. Console display name: "Link with PingOne User".
* `message` (string): The message to show to the user. Console display name: "Message".
* `mfaPolicyId` (string): The ID of the MFA Policy to use during flow execution, such as "aa4b3e81-cf7e-8685-4b7b-7ec89cfcf7c8". If this value is empty or invalid at runtime, the default MFA policy is used. Console display name: "MFA Policy ID".
* `nextEvent` (string): Console display name: "".
* `pingIdDesktopCredentialCreationOptions` (string): Select the pingIdDesktopCredentialCreationOptions variable from the PingOne MFA > Create Device capability. Console display name: "PingID Desktop Credential Creation Options".
* `pingIdDesktopCredentialRequestOptions` (string): Select the pingIdDesktopCredentialRequestOptions variable from the PingOne MFA > Create Device Authentication capability. Console display name: "PingID Desktop Credential Request Options".
* `pingidAgent` (string): When enabled, the Signals SDK collects attributes from the PingID Device Trust Agent. Console display name: "Enable PingID Agent".
* `pingidAgentPort` (string): The port number to use when connecting to the PingID Device Trust Agent. If left blank, the default port 9400 will be used. Console display name: "PingID Agent Port".
* `pingidAgentTimeout` (string): The time, in milliseconds, for establishing a connection with the PingID Device Trust Agent. If left blank, the default value is set by the Signals SDK. If specified, the value must be between 200 and 10,000 milliseconds. Console display name: "PingID Agent Timeout (ms)".
* `pollChallengeStatus` (string): When enabled, the form remains on the screen while DaVinci polls a challenge variable in another branch of the flow. When disabled, the flow continues past the form and loops at the next Continue Polling node. Console display name: "".
* `pollInterval` (string): The amount of time in milliseconds to wait between each polling status check. Console display name: "".
* `pollRetries` (string): The maximum number of times to check the polling status before failing, such as 60. Console display name: "".
* `pollingSectionLabel` (string): Console display name: "Polling".
* `population` (string): The PingOne population to use when authenticating the user. Console display name: "PingOne Population".
* `populationId` (string): The ID of the PingOne population to use when authenticating the user, such as “aa4b3e81-cf7e-8685-4b7b-7ec89cfcf7c8”. Console display name: "Population ID".
* `publicKeyCredentialCreationOptions` (string): Select the PublicKeyCredentialCreationOptions variable from the PingOne MFA > Create Device capability. Console display name: "Public Key Credential Creation Options".
* `publicKeyCredentialRequestOptions` (string): Select the PublicKeyCredentialRequestOptions variable from the PingOne MFA > Create Device Authentication capability. Console display name: "Public Key Credential Request Options".
* `qrCodeContents` (string): The URL, app link, code, or other string to represent in the QR code, such as "https://example.com", "myapp://section/page", or “123a-45b-678c". Console display name: "QR Code Contents".
* `qrCodeSectionLabel` (string): Console display name: "QR Code".
* `returnUrl` (string): When using the embedded flow player widget and an IdP/Social Login connector, provide a callback URL to return back to the application. Console display name: "Application Return URL".
* `returnUrlLabel` (string): Console display name: "Social Login".
* `routeClientErrorsToFalseBranch` (string): Route client-side errors (for example, NotAllowedError, AbortError, etc.) to the False branch in the error object. When disabled, errors are returned on the True branch as the buttonValue outcome. Console display name: "Route Client Errors to the False Branch".
* `sectionLabelFido2` (string): Console display name: "FIDO2".
* `sectionLabelPingIDDesktopApp` (string): Console display name: "PingID Desktop App".
* `showContinueButton` (string): When enabled, the user interface includes a button that allows the user to continue the flow. Console display name: "".
* `theme` (string): Choose a form theme from the themes configured in PingOne environment or use a Theme ID. If no theme is selected, the default active theme will be displayed. Console display name: "Form Theme".
* `themeId` (string): The ID of the PingOne theme to use when rendering the form, such as “aa4b3e81-cf7e-8685-4b7b-7ec89cfcf7c8”. Console display name: "Theme ID".
* `universalDeviceIdentification` (string): Identify the device via a unique device ID combined with a digital signature that ensures information collected about the device has not been tampered with. Console display name: "Enable Universal Device Identification".
* `userId` (string): The ID of the user to authenticate, such as "488e2f16-b765-4620-833d-f673669fecf6". Console display name: "User ID".

## Forter

Connector ID (`connector.id` in the resource): `forterConnector`

Properties (used under the `properties` block in the resource as a key in the JSON object):

* `accessRequestType` (string): Type of restricted access user is asking for. Console display name: "Access Request Type".
* `accountId` (string): Customer's account UID in merchant's site. Should not be the user email. Console display name: "Account ID".
* `accountIdSignup` (string): Customer's account UID in merchant's site. Should not be the user email. If no account ID is available, leave blank. Console display name: "Account ID".
* `accountType` (string): Account type (a business account, a private account, a merchant-operated account). Console display name: "Account Type".
* `apiVersion` (string): API Version. Console display name: " Forter API Version".
* `body` (string): This property needs to be a properly formatted JSON value. It can contain DaVinci parameters, which will be replaced at runtime. If you are using DaVinci parameters that are of type 'string', you will need to put string quotes around it. Console display name: "HTTP Body (JSON)".
* `correlationId` (string): A forter unique identifier that was provided as part of a Forter API response recommending additional authentication measures. Used to correlate between the user action which triggered the recommendation and the authentication attempt result. Required when the additional authentication was triggered by Forter's recommendation. Console display name: "Correlation ID".
* `endpoint` (string): The Forter API endpiont, such as "accounts/signup/${accountId}". Console display name: "Endpoint".
* `eventTimestamp` (string): The time that the trigger event occurred in MILLISECONDS since unix epoch (Jan 1, 1970). Console display name: "Event Timestamp".
* `forterTokenCookie` (string): Forter token cookie from request headers. Console display name: "Forter Token Cookie".
* `headers` (string): Add HTTP headers and provide their values. Console display name: "Headers".
* `inputType` (string): The type of identifier used by the user to login. Console display name: "Input Type".
* `ipAddress` (string): Customer IP address in IPv4 or IPv6 format. If missing should be populated with 127.0.0.1. Console display name: "IP Address".
* `loginMethodType` (string): The authentication method used to login. Console display name: "Login Method Type".
* `loginStatus` (string): The status of the login attempt. Console display name: "Login Status".
* `method` (string): The HTTP Method. Console display name: "Method".
* `queryParameters` (string): Add query parameters and provide their values. Console display name: "Query Parameters".
* `secretKey` (string): Secret Key from Forter tenant. Console display name: "Forter Secret Key".
* `siteId` (string): Site ID from Forter tenant. Console display name: "Forter SiteID".
* `status` (string): Account status. Console display name: "Status".
* `statusChangeBy` (string): The entity responsible for triggering the status change. Console display name: "Status Change By".
* `statusChangeReason` (string): The reason for the account status change. Required in case the update includes an account status change. Console display name: "Status Change Reason".
* `userAgent` (string): Customer's User agent. Console display name: "User Agent".

## Freshdesk

Connector ID (`connector.id` in the resource): `connectorFreshdesk`

Properties (used under the `properties` block in the resource as a key in the JSON object):

* `apiKey` (string): Make sure that the "APIkey:X" is Base64-encoded before pasting into the text field. Console display name: "Freshdesk API Key".
* `baseURL` (string): The <tenant>.freshdesk.com URL or custom domain. Console display name: "Freshdesk Base URL (or Domain)".
* `contactAddress` (string): Address of the contact. Console display name: "Address".
* `contactId` (string): The "contactId" listed under the output object. Console display name: "Contact ID".
* `contactJobTitle` (string): Job title of the contact. Console display name: "Job Title".
* `contactName` (string): First and last name of the new contact. Console display name: "Name".
* `contactPhone` (string): Telephone number of the contact. Console display name: "Phone Number".
* `email` (string): Email address of the requester. If no contact exists with this email address in Freshdesk, it will be added as a new contact. Console display name: "Email".
* `ticketDescription` (string): HTML content of the ticket. Console display name: "Description".
* `ticketId` (string): The numerical ID of the desired ticket. Can be found manually in your Freshdesk portal (i.e. 5 is the ID for “Ticket Title #5”). Console display name: "Ticket ID".
* `ticketPriority` (string): Priority of the ticket. The default value is 1. Console display name: "Priority".
* `ticketStatus` (string): Status of the ticket. The default value is 2. Console display name: "Status".
* `ticketSubject` (string): Subject of the Freshdesk ticket. Console display name: "Subject".
* `version` (string): The current Freshdesk API Version. Console display name: "Freshdesk API Version".

## Freshservice

Connector ID (`connector.id` in the resource): `connectorFreshservice`

Properties (used under the `properties` block in the resource as a key in the JSON object):

* `address` (string): Address of the requester. Console display name: "Address".
* `apiKey` (string): Your Freshservice API key. Console display name: "API Key".
* `backgroundInformation` (string): Background information of the requester. Console display name: "Background Information".
* `canSeeAllTicketsFromAssociatedDepts` (string): Set to true if the requester must be allowed to view tickets filed by other members of the department, and false otherwise. Console display name: "Can See All Tickets From Associate Departments".
* `ccEmails` (string): Email address added in the 'cc' field of the incoming ticket email. Must be comma-separated list of emails. Console display name: "CC Emails (comma-separated)".
* `departmentIds` (string): Unique IDs of the departments associated with the requester.  Must be comma-separated. Console display name: "DepartmentIds (comma-separated)".
* `description` (string): HTML content of the ticket. Console display name: "Description".
* `domain` (string): Your Freshservice domain. Example: https://domain.freshservice.com/. Console display name: "Domain".
* `dueBy` (string): Timestamp that denotes when the ticket is due to be resolved. Console display name: "Due By".
* `email` (string): Email address of the requester. If no contact exists with this email address in Freshservice, it will be added as a new contact. Console display name: "Email".
* `emailConfigId` (string): ID of email config which is used for this ticket. (i.e., support@yourcompany.com/sales@yourcompany.com) If product_id is given and email_config_id is not given, product's primary email_config_id will be set. Console display name: "Email Config ID".
* `firstName` (string): First name of the requester. Console display name: "First Name".
* `frDueBy` (string): Timestamp that denotes when the first response is due. Console display name: "FR Due By".
* `groupId` (string): ID of the group to which the ticket has been assigned. The default value is the ID of the group that is associated with the given email_config_id. Console display name: "Group ID".
* `impact` (string): Ticket impact. Console display name: "Impact".
* `jobTitle` (string): Job title of the requester. Console display name: "Job Title".
* `language` (string): Language used by the requester. The default language is “en” (English). https://support.freshservice.com/support/solutions/articles/232303-list-of-languages-supported-in-freshservice. Console display name: "Language".
* `lastName` (string): Last name of the connector. Console display name: "Last Name".
* `locationId` (string): Unique ID of the location associated with the requester. Console display name: "Location ID".
* `mobilePhoneNumber` (string): Mobile phone number of the requester. Console display name: "Mobile Phone Number".
* `name` (string): Name of the requester. Console display name: "Name".
* `phone` (string): Phone number of the requester. If no contact exists with this phone number in Freshservice, it will be added as a new contact. If the phone number is set and the email address is not, then the name attribute is mandatory. Console display name: "Phone".
* `primaryEmail` (string): Primary email address of the requester. Console display name: "Primary Email".
* `priority` (string): Priority of the ticket. The default value is 1. Console display name: "Priority".
* `reportingManagerId` (string): User ID of the requester's reporting manager. Console display name: "Reporting Manager ID".
* `requesterId` (string): User ID of the requester. Console display name: "Requester ID".
* `responderId` (string): ID of the agent to whom the ticket has been assigned. Console display name: "Responder ID".
* `secondaryEmails` (string): Additional/secondary emails associated with the requester.  Must be comma-separated. Console display name: "Secondary Emails (comma-separated)".
* `source` (string): The channel through which the ticket was created. The default value is 2. Console display name: "Source".
* `status` (string): Status of the ticket. The default Value is 2. Console display name: "Status".
* `subject` (string): Subject of the ticket. The default Value is null. Console display name: "Subject".
* `tags` (string): Tags that have been associated with the ticket. Must be comma-separated. Console display name: "Tags (comma-separated)".
* `ticketId` (string): The ticket ID. Console display name: "Ticket ID".
* `timeFormat` (string): Time format for the requester. Possible values: 12h (12 hour format), 24h (24 hour format). Console display name: "Time Format".
* `timeZone` (string): Time zone of the requester. https://support.freshservice.com/support/solutions/articles/232302-list-of-time-zones-supported-in-freshservice. Console display name: "Time Zone".
* `urgency` (string): Ticket urgency. Console display name: "Urgency".
* `workPhoneNumber` (string): Work phone number of the requester. Console display name: "Work Phone Number".


Example:

```terraform
resource "pingone_davinci_connector_instance" "connectorFreshservice" {
  environment_id = var.pingone_environment_id

  connector = {
    id = "connectorFreshservice"
  }
  name = "My awesome connectorFreshservice"
  property {
    name  = "address"
    type  = "string"
```

## Functions

Connector ID (`connector.id` in the resource): `functionsConnector`

Properties (used under the `properties` block in the resource as a key in the JSON object):

* `caseSensitive` (string): When enabled, the values are considered a match only if the case is the same. Console display name: "Case Sensitive".
* `checkNullORUndefined` (string): Check undefined/null. Console display name: "Check undefined/null".
* `code` (string): Follow example for code. Caution: Custom code is for advanced users only. Before using custom code, review the security risks in the DaVinci documentation by searching for "Using custom code safely". Console display name: "".
* `customSaltValue` (string): Enter the salt value to use when hashing, such as “mySaltu7v8w9x0“. Console display name: "Custom Salt Value".
* `digestAlgorithm` (string): The hash algorithm to use. Console display name: "Hash Algorithm".
* `inputContains` (string): Console display name: "".
* `leftValueA` (string): Console display name: "".
* `message` (string): The value to hash, such as “myPa55woRd123#". Console display name: "Input Value".
* `outputEncodingFormat` (string): The encoding method for the resulting hashed value. Console display name: "Output Encoding Format".
* `outputSchema` (string): Follow example for JSON schema. Console display name: "".
* `rightValueB` (string): Console display name: "".
* `rightValueC` (string): Console display name: "".
* `rightValueMultiple` (string): Console display name: "".
* `saltMode` (string): Determines whether to add a salt value to make the hashed value unique and more difficult to guess. For a custom value, select Use Custom Salt Value and enter the value in Custom Salt Value. Console display name: "Salt Mode".
* `type` (string): Console display name: "".
* `variableInputList` (string): Console display name: "".

Console display name: "Encrypted_value".

You can only provide a list of repository ids when the &#x60;visibility&#x60; is set to &#x60;selected&#x60;. You can manage the list of selected repositories using the [List selected repositories for an organization secret](https://docs.github.com/enterprise-server@3.1/rest/reference/actions#list-selected-repositories-for-an-organization-secret), [Set selected repositories for an organization secret](https://docs.github.com/enterprise-server@3.1/rest/reference/actions#set-selected-repositories-for-an-organization-secret), and [Remove selected repository from an organization secret](https://docs.github.com/enterprise-server@3.1/rest/reference/actions#remove-selected-repository-from-an-organization-secret) endpoints. * `checksCreate_checksCreateRequest_ChecksCreateRequestOutput_annotations` (string): Adds information from your analysis to specific lines of code. Annotations are visible on GitHub in the **Checks** and **Files changed** tab of the pull request. The Checks API limits the number of annotations to a maximum of 50 per API request. To create more than 50 annotations, you have to make multiple requests to the [Update a check run](https://docs.github.com/enterprise-server@3.1/rest/reference/checks#update-a-check-run) endpoint. Each time you update the check run, annotations are appended to the list of annotations that already exist for the check run. For details about how you can view annotations on GitHub, see &quot;[About status checks](https://docs.github.com/articles/about-status-checks#checks)&quot;. See the [&#x60;annotations&#x60; object](https://docs.github.com/enterprise-server@3.1/rest/reference/checks#annotations-object) description for details about how to use this parameter. Console display name: "Annotations".
* `checksCreate_checksCreateRequest_ChecksCreateRequestOutput_images` (string): Adds images to the output displayed in the GitHub pull request UI. See the [&#x60;images&#x60; object](https://docs.github.com/enterprise-server@3.1/rest/reference/checks#images-object) description for details. Console display name: "Images".
* `checksCreate_checksCreateRequest_ChecksCreateRequestOutput_summary` (string): The summary of the check run. This parameter supports Markdown. Console display name: "Summary".
* `checksCreate_checksCreateRequest_ChecksCreateRequestOutput_text` (string): The details of the check run. This parameter supports Markdown. Console display name: "Text".
* `checksCreate_checksCreateRequest_ChecksCreateRequestOutput_title` (string): The title of the check run. Console display name: "Title".
* `checksCreate_checksCreateRequest_ChecksCreateRequest_actions` (string): Displays a button on GitHub that can be clicked to alert your app to do additional tasks. For example, a code linting app can display a button that automatically fixes detected errors. The button created in this object is displayed after the check run completes. When a user clicks the button, GitHub sends the [&#x60;check_run.requested_action&#x60; webhook](https://docs.github.com/enterprise-server@3.1/webhooks/event-payloads/#check_run) to your app. Each action includes a &#x60;label&#x60;, &#x60;identifier&#x60; and &#x60;description&#x60;. A maximum of three actions are accepted. See the [&#x60;actions&#x60; object](https://docs.github.com/enterprise-server@3.1/rest/reference/checks#actions-object) description. Use &#x60;RIGHT&#x60; for additions that appear in green or unchanged lines that appear in white and are shown for context. For a multi-line comment, side represents whether the last line of the comment range is a deletion or addition. For more information, see &quot;[Diff view options](https://docs.github.com/en/articles/about-comparing-branches-in-pull-requests#diff-view-options)&quot; in the GitHub Help documentation. To learn more about multi-line comments, see &quot;[Commenting on a pull request](https://docs.github.com/en/articles/commenting-on-a-pull-request#adding-line-comments-to-a-pull-request)&quot; in the GitHub Help documentation. Can be &#x60;LEFT&#x60; or &#x60;RIGHT&#x60;. To learn more about multi-line comments, see &quot;[Commenting on a pull request](https://docs.github.com/en/articles/commenting-on-a-pull-request#adding-line-comments-to-a-pull-request)&quot; in the GitHub Help documentation. ## GitHub Login

Connector ID (`connector.id` in the resource): `githubIdpConnector`

Properties (used under the `properties` block in the resource as a key in the JSON object):

* `authType` (string): Console display name: "".
* `button` (string): Console display name: "Login with GitHub".
* `oauth2` (string): Console display name: "".
* `showPoweredBy` (string): Console display name: "".


Example:
```terraform
resource "pingone_davinci_connector_instance" "githubIdpConnector" {
  environment_id = var.pingone_environment_id

  connector = {
    id = "githubIdpConnector"
  }
  name = "My awesome githubIdpConnector"
  property {
    name  = "authType"
    type  = "string"
    value = var.githubidpconnector_property_auth_type
  }
  property {
    name  = "button"
    type  = "string"
    value = var.githubidpconnector_property_button
  }
  property {
    name  = "oauth2"
    type  = "string"
    value = jsonencode({})
  }
  property {
    name  = "showPoweredBy"
    type  = "string"
    value = var.githubidpconnector_property_show_powered_by
  }
}
```
