## Google Workspace Admin

Connector ID (`connector.id` in the resource): `googleWorkSpaceAdminConnector`

Properties (used under the `properties` block in the resource as a key in the JSON object):

* `action` (string): The administrative action to take on the device. Console display name: "Action".
* `additionalUserProperties` (string): Define additional attributes to add to the user account. For help, see the User Accounts section of the Google Workspace SDK documentation. Console display name: "Other User Attributes".
* `bodyData` (string): The body of the API call. Console display name: "Body".
* `customerId` (string): The unique ID for the customer's Google Workspace account, such as "C123abc4d". This ID is available from the "Get User Information" capability. Console display name: "Customer ID".
* `deviceProjection` (string): The level of information to request about the device. "Basic" returns a standard set of fields. "Full" returns all fields. Console display name: "Requested Device Fields".
* `endpoint` (string): The Workspace API endpoint, such as "https://admin.googleapis.com/admin/directory/v1/users/user@example.com". Console display name: "Endpoint".
* `familyName` (string): The user's last name.  Console display name: "Family Name".
* `givenName` (string): The user's given name. Console display name: "Given Name".
* `groupKey` (string): The group's primary email address, unique group id, or alias. Console display name: "Group Identifier".
* `headersForm` (string): Define additional headers to send to Workspace. For help, see the Google Workspace API documentation. Console display name: "Additional Headers".
* `iss` (string): The email address associated with the Google Workspace service, such as "google-workspace-admin@xenon-set-123456.iam.gserviceaccount.com". Console display name: "Service Account Email Address".
* `licenseUserId` (string): The user's primary email address. Console display name: "User ID".
* `maxResults` (string): The maximum number of results to return from the query, up to 100. Console display name: "Maximum Number of Results".
* `memberDeliverySettings` (string): The member's email delivery frequency.  Console display name: "Member Email Delivery Settings".
* `memberEmail` (string): The member's email address. The member can be a user or another group. Console display name: "Member Email".
* `memberKey` (string): Identifies the group member in the API request. Console display name: "Member Key".
* `memberRole` (string): The role to assign the member in the group. Console display name: "Member Role".
* `memberType` (string): The type of member in the group. Console display name: "Member Type".
* `method` (string): The HTTP method of the API call. Console display name: "HTTP Method".
* `orderBy` (string): The device property to use for sorting results. Console display name: "Device Order".
* `pageToken` (string): The token used to specify the next page in the results, such as "3". Use this to get pages of results for queries that return more than the maximum number of results.
 Console display name: "Page Token".
* `paramsForm` (string): Query parameters for the request. Console display name: "Query Parameters".
* `password` (string): The password to assign to the user account. Console display name: "Password".
* `primaryEmail` (string): The user's primary email address. Console display name: "Primary Email".
* `privateKey` (string): The private key associated with the public key that you added to the Google Workspace service. Console display name: "Private Key".
* `productId` (string): The product ID, such as "Google-Apps". Console display name: "Product ID".
* `projection` (string): The level of information to request about the user. "Basic" returns a standard set of fields. "Full" returns all fields. "Use Custom Field Schemas" returns the Basic fields as well as specific fields associated with the schemas you enter in "Custom Field Schemas". Console display name: "Requested Fields".
* `query` (string): The query used to search for devices, such as "status:approved" or "os:Android". For help, see documentation for "Mobile device search fields" section of the Google Workspace SDK Directory API documentation.
 Console display name: "Query String".
* `resourceId` (string): The device ID, such as "AFiQxQ-WO…YM-hf080OZy". Console display name: "Device ID".
* `skuId` (string): The SKU ID, such as "Google-Apps-For-Business". Console display name: "SKU ID".
* `sortOrder` (string): The sort order for the list of devices. This is required if you have selected a "Device Order" option. Console display name: "Sort Order".
* `sub` (string): The administrator's email address. Console display name: "Admin Email Address".
* `userCustomFieldMask` (string): The list of schemas to request. This returns all fields associated with the listed schemas. Type a schema name and press Enter to add it. Console display name: "Custom Field Schemas".
* `userFieldMask` (string): The list of fields for the connector to output to the flow, such as "emails" or "emails.address". Instead of outputting all of the results from the "Requested Attributes", you can filter the results to a list of specific fields. Type a field name and press Enter to add it. Leave this field blank to include all requested fields in the connector output. Console display name: "Output Filter".
* `userKey` (string): The user's primary email address, unique user id, or one of the user's alias email addresses.
 Console display name: "User Identifier".
* `viewType` (string): The type of fields to request. "Admin View" returns publicly visible and administrator-only fields. "Public View" only returns publicly visible fields. Console display name: "View Type".

## HTTP

Connector ID (`connector.id` in the resource): `httpConnector`

Properties (used under the `properties` block in the resource as a key in the JSON object):

* `additionalFieldsName` (string): Console display name: "".
* `blockRedirects` (string): When enabled, DaVinci enhances the security of the flow by preventing the browser from automatically following redirects and an error occurs instead. Console display name: "Block Redirects".
* `bodyHeaderText` (string): Form body title. Console display name: "".
* `bodyParams` (string): Console display name: "Body Params".
* `button` (string): Console display name: "Submit".
* `challenge` (string): Console display name: "".
* `claimsNameValuePairs` (string): Use this section to add additional fields to the response. Console display name: "Additional Fields in the Response".
* `connectionId` (string): Console display name: "Select an OpenID token management connection for signed HTTP responses.".
* `connectionInstanceId` (string): In advanced scenarios, it might be required to specify the Node ID of the UI node where polling in enabled. When a Node ID is not entered (default behavior), polling will continue on the current UI node. Console display name: "Node ID of the UI node (Optional)".
* `contentSource` (string): Select the source of the HTML, CSS, & Script content. Console display name: "Content Source".
* `contentType` (string): Content Type of the response data. To apply output schema content type must be application/json. Console display name: "Success Response Content Type".
* `contentTypeError` (string): Content Type of the response data. To apply output schema content type must be application/json. Console display name: "Error Response Content Type".
* `customCSS` (string): Console display name: "CSS".
* `customCSSByCdn` (string): Enter the CDN URL that hosts the CSS you would like to use. The CDN hostname must be listed in the Trusted Sites under the connector settings. Console display name: "CSS CDN URL".
* `customHTML` (string): Console display name: "HTML Template".
* `customHTMLByCdn` (string): Enter the CDN URL that hosts the HTML you would like to use. The CDN hostname must be listed in the Trusted Sites under the connector settings. Console display name: "HTML CDN URL".
* `customScript` (string): Write custom JavaScript. Caution: Custom code is for advanced users only. Before using custom code, review the security risks in the DaVinci documentation by searching for "Using custom code safely". Console display name: "Script".
* `customScriptByCdn` (string): Enter the CDN URL that hosts the Javascript you would like to use. The CDN hostname must be listed in the Trusted Sites under the connector settings. Console display name: "Script CDN URL".
* `customUrl` (string): Console display name: "URL".
* `delayTime` (string): Time to wait for response to be sent in milliseconds. Default: 50. Console display name: "Delay Time (ms)".
* `description` (string): Console display name: "Add form fields that you would wish the user to populate.".
* `enablePolling` (string): Console display name: "Enable Polling?".
* `fieldValidation` (string): The flow will fail if the validation is failed. Console display name: "Validate the additional properties".
* `formFieldsList` (string): Console display name: "".
* `headers` (string): Console display name: "Headers".
* `httpBody` (string): Console display name: "Body".
* `httpHeaders` (string): Console display name: "".
* `httpMethod` (string): Console display name: "HTTP Method".
* `httpStatusCode` (string): Console display name: "".
* `inputSchema` (string): Follow example for JSON schema. Console display name: "".
* `jsonString` (string): This property needs to be a properly formatted JSON value. It can contain DaVinci parameters, which will be replaced at runtime. If you are using DaVinci parameters that are of type 'string', you will need to put string quotes around it. Console display name: "HTTP Body (JSON)".
* `keepOutputIfNotValid` (string): Console display name: "Keep API output if the validation failed".
* `message` (string): Console display name: "".
* `messageIcon` (string): Console display name: "Message Icon URL".
* `messageIconHeight` (string): Console display name: "Message Icon Height (in pixels)".
* `messageTitle` (string): Console display name: "".
* `nextButtonText` (string): Console display name: "".
* `nextEvent` (string): Console display name: "".
* `outboundMtlsKey` (string): Select the client certificate used to make outbound mTLS connections. Console display name: "MTLS Support".
* `outputSchema` (string): Follow example for JSON schema. Console display name: "".
* `outputSchemaError` (string): Follow example for JSON schema. Console display name: "".
* `pollChallengeStatus` (string): Console display name: "".
* `pollInterval` (string): Console display name: "".
* `pollRetries` (string): Console display name: "".
* `queryParams` (string): Console display name: "Query Params".
* `raw` (string): Input your raw request body. Console display name: "raw".
* `recaptchaSecretKey` (string): The Secret Key from reCAPTCHA Admin dashboard. Console display name: "reCAPTCHA v2 Secret Key".
* `recaptchaSiteKey` (string): The Site Key from reCAPTCHA Admin dashboard. Console display name: "reCAPTCHA v2 Site Key".
* `returnRequestParameters` (string): Console display name: "".
* `returnSuccess` (string): Return success or failure response. Console display name: "Return Success Response".
* `showContinueButton` (string): Console display name: "".
* `showFooter` (string): Console display name: "".
* `showPoweredBy` (string): Console display name: "".
* `signResponse` (string): Sign the response as JWT using your company's private keys. Signatures can be validated using JWKS public keys in the Company section. Console display name: "Signed Response".
* `sktemplate` (string): Console display name: "Template".
* `timeout` (string): The amount of time in milliseconds before the request times out, such as "3000". Leave blank to use the maximum timeout of 29000 ms. Console display name: "Timeout (ms)".
* `title` (string): Form title. Console display name: "".
* `unsafeIgnoreTLSErrors` (string): When enabled, the connector ignores TLS errors. Use this for testing in non-production environments. Console display name: "Ignore TLS Errors".
* `url` (string): Console display name: "URL".
* `useRecaptcha` (string): Add sk-component skrecaptcha to use this feature. Console display name: "Use Recaptcha Verification".
* `validationRules` (string): Rules to check to validate form inputs. Console display name: "Form validation rules".
* `validity` (string): Expiry time in milliseconds. Default is 86400000 (1 day). Console display name: "Validity".
* `whiteList` (string): Enter the hostname for the trusted sites that host your HTML. Note: Ensure that the content hosted on these sites can be trusted and that publishing safeguards are in place to prevent unexpected issues. Console display name: "Trusted Sites".

## Hubspot

Connector ID (`connector.id` in the resource): `connectorHubspot`

Properties (used under the `properties` block in the resource as a key in the JSON object):

* `associationType` (string): The Type of the association you wish to create. Console display name: "Type of association".
* `bearerToken` (string): Your unique API key. Console display name: "API Key".
* `body` (string): The raw JSON body, such as "{ "Username": "jsmith@example.com", "ProfileId": "00e8a0000024zkjAAA" }". Console display name: "Body".
* `company` (string): Company of a contact. Console display name: "Company".
* `contactID` (string): Unique ID number of a contact. Console display name: "Contact ID".
* `email` (string): Email of a contact. Console display name: "Email".
* `endpoint` (string): The Hubspot API endpoint, such as "/crm/v3/extensions/accounting/settings/{appId}". Console display name: "Endpoint".
* `fname` (string): First name of a contact. Console display name: "First Name".
* `headers` (string): Add HTTP headers and provide their values. Console display name: "Headers".
* `hubspotOwnerID` (string): The unique ID number for the owner of the ticket. Console display name: "Owner ID".
* `lname` (string): Last name of a contact. Console display name: "Last Name".
* `method` (string): The HTTP Method. Console display name: "Method".
* `phone` (string): Phone number of a contact. Console display name: "Phone".
* `queryParameters` (string): Add query parameters and provide their values. Console display name: "Query Parameters".
* `subject` (string): The subject of the ticket. Console display name: "Ticket Subject".
* `ticketID` (string): Unique ID number of a ticket. Console display name: "Ticket ID".
* `ticketPipeline` (string): The pipeline you'd like to create the ticket in. Console display name: "Ticket pipeline".
* `ticketPriority` (string): Priority Level of the ticket (ex. LOW, MED, HIGH). Console display name: "Ticket Priority".
* `ticketStage` (string): The stage of the ticket (ex. 1, 2, 3, etc.). Console display name: "Ticket Stage".
* `toObjectID` (string): To object ID (the unique ID number of the object you are associating To). Console display name: "To object ID".
* `toObjectType` (string): Type of the object you are associating TO. Console display name: "To object type (ex. Company, etc.)".
* `website` (string): Website of a contact. Console display name: "Website".

## IDEMIA

Properties (used under the `properties` block in the resource as a key in the JSON object):

* `customCSS` (string): Console display name: "CSS".
* `customHTML` (string): Console display name: "HTML Template".

* `documentId` (string): REQUIRED. The ID for uploaded document in process for verification. Console display name: "Document ID".
* `htmlConfig` (string): Console display name: "".
* `identitiesId` (string): REQUIRED. The ID of identities that was created from Create Identities capability. Console display name: "Identities ID".
* `livenessMode` (string): REQUIRED. The liveness mode type for liveness verification. Console display name: "Liveness Mode".
* `portraitConsent` (string): Submit confirmation that user consent has been obtained to perform specific evidence verifications for a given period. Console display name: "Consent to Portrait".
* `portraitId` (string): REQUIRED. The ID for uploaded portrait in process for verification. Console display name: "Portrait ID".
* `portraitValidDate` (string): The period for which the consent is considered valid. Will be added automatically by the service if not provided. Console display name: "Portrait Consent Valid Till".
* `useCustomScreens` (string): Console display name: "Use Custom Screens".

## Intellicheck

Connector ID (`connector.id` in the resource): `intellicheckConnector`

Properties (used under the `properties` block in the resource as a key in the JSON object):

* `apiKey` (string): API Key from your Intellicheck tenant. Console display name: "API Key".
* `baseUrl` (string): Base URL from your Intellicheck tenant (Including protocol - https://). Console display name: "Base URL".
* `customerId` (string): Customer ID from your Intellicheck tenant. Console display name: "Customer ID".
* `deviceValidation` (string): If ON, device fingerprinting and IP address validation fields are returned in the results. If OFF, they are not. Console display name: "Device Validation".
* `documentTypeSelection` (string): Identification type. Values: na_dl, passport, other. Select only one. If you specify na_dl, then at a minimum, you must include the idcheck signal. Likewise, if you select passport or other, then at a minimum, you must include the ocr_scan signal. If these minimum signal requirements are not specified in your request body, then they will be used by default. Console display name: "Document Type".
* `intellicheckErrorRedirectUrl` (string): An error redirect can occur if the end user does not complete the capture process, for example, if the end user declines camera access. Another example is if the end user does not complete the capture process in time, as defined by the ttl property of the private_data object. The default ttl value is 10 minutes. After an error, this URL loads in the browser, redirecting the end user. Use HTTPS in the URL with a fully qualified domain. Console display name: "Error Redirect URL".
* `intellicheckRedirectUrl` (string): A redirect can occur at the completion of the capture process. For example, this redirect URL could load your company's webpage to the end user browser. Use HTTPS in the URL with a fully qualified domain. Console display name: "Redirect URL".
* `phoneNumber` (string): End user's phone number. Console display name: "Phone Number".
* `signals` (string): Array of Signals to run for this transaction that is verified against the subscribed list. Possible values include document_liveness_idrnd, idcheck, ocr_match, ocr_scan, and selfie. Leave blank to request all signals to which you are subscribed. Console display name: "Signals".
* `transactionId` (string): ID issued at the beginning of a transaction to associate all subsequent processes within the transaction until ended. Console display name: "Transaction ID".
* `ttl` (string): Override of the default minutes to complete. Maximum value is 30. Console display name: "TTL".


Example:
```terraform
resource "pingone_davinci_connector_instance" "intellicheckConnector" {
  environment_id = var.pingone_environment_id

  connector = {
    id = "intellicheckConnector"
  }
  name = "My awesome intellicheckConnector"
  property {
    name  = "apiKey"
    type  = "string"
    value = var.intellicheckconnector_property_api_key
  }
  property {
    name  = "baseUrl"
    type  = "string"
    value = var.intellicheckconnector_property_base_url
  }
  property {
    name  = "customerId"
    type  = "string"
    value = var.intellicheckconnector_property_customer_id
  }
  property {
    name  = "deviceValidation"
    type  = "string"
    value = var.intellicheckconnector_property_device_validation
  }
  property {
    name  = "documentTypeSelection"
    type  = "string"
    value = var.intellicheckconnector_property_document_type_selection
  }
  property {
    name  = "intellicheckErrorRedirectUrl"
    type  = "string"
    value = var.intellicheckconnector_property_intellicheck_error_redirect_url
  }
  property {
    name  = "intellicheckRedirectUrl"
    type  = "string"
    value = var.intellicheckconnector_property_intellicheck_redirect_url
  }
  property {
    name  = "phoneNumber"
    type  = "string"
    value = var.intellicheckconnector_property_phone_number
  }
  property {
    name  = "signals"
    type  = "string"
    value = var.intellicheckconnector_property_signals
  }
  property {
    name  = "transactionId"
    type  = "string"
    value = var.intellicheckconnector_property_transaction_id
  }
  property {
    name  = "ttl"
    type  = "string"
    value = var.intellicheckconnector_property_ttl
  }
}
```

## Jira

Connector ID (`connector.id` in the resource): `jiraConnector`

Properties (used under the `properties` block in the resource as a key in the JSON object):

* `apiKey` (string): You may need to create a token from Jira with your credentials, if you haven't created one. Console display name: "Jira API token".
* `apiUrl` (string): Base URL of the Jira instance. Console display name: "Base Url".
* `assignee` (string): The person to assign the issue to. For a dynamic value, select Use Assignee ID and enter a value in the Assignee ID field. Console display name: "Assignee".
* `assigneeId` (string): The ID of the assignee, such as "5b10a2844c20165700ede21g". Console display name: "Assignee ID".
* `bodyData` (string): The body of the API call. Console display name: "Body".
* `components` (string): The ID of the component to associate with the issue, such as "10000". Console display name: "Components".
* `customQueryParams` (string): Define additional query parameters to send to Jira. For help, see the Jira Cloud platform REST API documentation. Console display name: "Query Parameters".
* `description` (string): The issue description, such as "Please fix the following development workflow issue…". Console display name: "Description".
* `dueDate` (string): The due date for the issue, formatted as "2022-01-30". Console display name: "Due Date".
* `email` (string): Email used for your Jira account. Console display name: "Email Address".
* `endpoint` (string): The Jira API endpoint, such as /rest/api/3/search. Console display name: "Endpoint".
* `expand` (string): Additional information to get for the issues returned in the results, such as "names", "schema", or "changelog". For help, see "Search for issues with JQL (POST)" in the Jira Cloud platform REST API documentation. Console display name: "Expanded Information".
* `fields` (string): The fields to get for each issue returned in the results, such as "assignee" or "comment". Type a field name and press enter to add it. Console display name: "Fields".
* `fieldsByKeys` (string): Enable this when the "Fields" list uses keys, rather than IDs, to identify fields. Console display name: "Identify Fields with Keys".
* `fixVersions` (string): The ID of the fix version to associate with the issue, such as "10001". Type an ID and press Enter to add it. Console display name: "Fix Versions".
* `headers` (string): Additional headers for the request, connector automatically adds 'Authorization' and 'Content-Type' headers. Console display name: "Additional Headers".
* `issueId` (string): The ID of the issue, such as "PROJ-1". Console display name: "Issue ID".
* `issueType` (string): The type of issue to create. Console display name: "Issue Type".
* `jql` (string): The JQL query used to search for issues, such as "project=SysAdmin AND assignee=jsmith". For help, see documentation for the Jira Query Language. Console display name: "JQL Query".
* `labels` (string): The labels to associate with the issue. Type a label and press enter to add it. Console display name: "Labels".
* `loopingTransition` (string): Enable this for transitions that start and end on the same status. Console display name: "Looping Transition".
* `maxResults` (number): The maximum number of results to return from the query. Use with Starting Result Number to get pages of results for queries that return more than the maximum number of results. Console display name: "Maximum Number of Results".
* `method` (string): The HTTP method of the API call. Console display name: "HTTP Method".
* `otherAttributes` (string): Add other attributes and their values. Will overwrite attributes in General tab if key is the same. Console display name: "Other Attributes".
* `parent` (string): The ID of an existing issue, such as "PROJ-10". When this value is provided, the new issue will be created as a sub-task of the parent issue. Console display name: "Parent Issue ID".
* `priority` (string): The priority for the issue, such as "3". Console display name: "Priority".
* `project` (string): The Jira project to create the issue in. For a dynamic value, select Use Project Key and enter a value in the Project Key field. Console display name: "Project".
* `projectKey` (string): The Jira project to create the issue in, such as "PROJ". Console display name: "Project Key".
* `queryParams` (string): Define additional query parameters to send to Jira. For help, see the Jira Cloud platform REST API documentation. Console display name: "Query Parameters".
* `reporter` (string): The person reporting the issue. For a dynamic value, select Use Reporter ID and enter a value in the Reporter ID field. Console display name: "Reporter".
* `reporterId` (string): The ID of the reporter, such as "5b10a2844c20165700ede21g". Console display name: "Reporter ID".
* `searchProperties` (string): The app or entity properties to get for each issue returned in the results. Type a property name and press enter to add it, to a maximum of five properties. Console display name: "Properties".
* `startAt` (number): The index number of the first item to return in the results. For example, "101" will return the maximum number of results starting with result number 101. Use this to get pages of results for queries that return more than the maximum number of results. Console display name: "Starting Result Number".
* `summary` (string): The issue summary, such as "Fix development workflow". Console display name: "Summary".
* `transitionId` (string): The ID of the transition to trigger. Console display name: "Transition ID".
* `updateIssueType` (string): The updated issue type. Console display name: "Issue Type".
* `updateSummary` (string): The issue summary, such as "Fix development workflow". Console display name: "Summary".
* `validateQuery` (string): The method to use to validate the JQL query. Console display name: "Query Validation".
* `versions` (string): The ID of the version to associate with the issue, such as "10001". Type an ID and press Enter to add it. Console display name: "Versions".


Example:

## Jira Service Desk

Connector ID (`connector.id` in the resource): `connectorJiraServiceDesk`

Properties (used under the `properties` block in the resource as a key in the JSON object):

* `JIRAServiceDeskAuth` (string): Bearer Authorization Token for JIRA Service Desk. Console display name: "Bearer Authorization Token for JIRA Service Desk".
* `JIRAServiceDeskCreateData` (string): Raw JSON body to create new JIRA service desk request. Example: {   "requestParticipants": ["qm:a713c8ea-1075-4e30-9d96-891a7d181739:5ad6d69abfa3980ce712caae"   ],   "serviceDeskId": "10",   "requestTypeId": "25",   "requestFieldValues": {     "summary": "Request JSD help via REST",     "description": "I need a new *mouse* for my Mac"   } }. Console display name: "Raw JSON for creating new JIRA service desk request".
* `JIRAServiceDeskIssueID` (string): Issue ID of JIRA service desk request. Console display name: "JIRA Service Desk Issue ID".
* `JIRAServiceDeskURL` (string): URL for JIRA Service Desk. Example: your-domain.atlassian.net. Console display name: "JIRA Service Desk URL".
* `JIRAServiceDeskUpdateData` (string): Raw JSON body to update JIRA service desk request. Example: {"id": "1","additionalComment": {"body": "I have fixed the problem."}}. Console display name: "Raw JSON for updating JIRA service desk".
* `body` (string): The raw JSON body, such as "{ "Username": "jsmith@example.com", "ProfileId": "00e8a0000024zkjAAA" }". Console display name: "Body".
* `endpoint` (string): The Jira Service Desk API endpoint, such as "/rest/api/3/<resource-name>". Console display name: "Endpoint".
* `headers` (string): Add HTTP headers and provide their values. Console display name: "Headers".
* `method` (string): The HTTP Method. Console display name: "Method".
* `queryParameters` (string): Add query parameters and provide their values. Console display name: "Query Parameters".

## LDAP

Connector ID (`connector.id` in the resource): `pingOneLDAPConnector`

Properties (used under the `properties` block in the resource as a key in the JSON object):

* `attributeName` (string): The name of the attribute that will be modified. Console display name: "Attribute Name".
* `attributes` (string): Console display name: "Attributes".
* `baseDN` (string): The base distinguished name of the search. Console display name: "Base DN".
* `bindDN` (string): Console display name: "Bind DN".
* `bindPassword` (string): Console display name: "Bind Password".
* `clientId` (string): The Client ID of your PingOne Worker application. Console display name: "Client ID".
* `clientSecret` (string): The Client Secret of your PingOne Worker application. Console display name: "Client Secret".
* `controls` (string): A JSON array of controls to include with this request. Console display name: "Controls".
* `dn` (string): The DN to perform the operation on. Console display name: "DN".
* `entryAttributes` (string): The attributes that should be retrieved. If "Retrieve Operational Attributes" is true, "*" must be used in order to retrieve all user attributes. Otherwise, retrieving all user attributes can be done by leaving this field blank. Console display name: "Entry Attributes".
* `envId` (string): Your PingOne environment ID. Console display name: "Environment ID".
* `filter` (string): The criteria for defining matching entries in a search. Console display name: "Filter".
* `gatewayId` (string): Your PingOne LDAP gateway ID. Console display name: "Gateway ID".
* `jsonAttributes` (string): Input attributes as a JSON object with the attribute names as the keys and the attribute values as the values. Multi-valued attributes may be provided as an array. Console display name: "Attributes".
* `ldapUrl` (string): Console display name: "LDAP URL".
* `modifications` (string): The attribute values to add or delete. Multiple modifications with the same operation may be specified in order to manage multiple values at once. Console display name: "Modifications".
* `newDn` (string): The new DN of the entry. Console display name: "New DN".
* `newPassword` (string): The password to set on an entry. Console display name: "New Password".
* `oldPassword` (string): The current password for the entry. If provided, it must match the entry's current password in order for the operation to succeed. Console display name: "Old Password".
* `password` (string): The user's password to validate. Console display name: "Password".
* `proxyAuthzDn` (string): The Distinguished Name of the user to perform this operation as. Console display name: "Proxied Authorization DN".
* `proxyAuthzUser` (string): The user that will perform this operation. Console display name: "Perform Operation As".
* `proxyAuthzUsername` (string): The user to perform this operation as. Console display name: "Proxied Authorization Username".
* `region` (string): The region in which your PingOne environment exists. Console display name: "Region".
* `retrieveOperationalAttributes` (string): Operational attributes will be retrieved when this is enabled. If you wish to retrieve all user attributes in addition to operational attributes, "*" must be specified in the "Entry Attributes" field. Console display name: "Retrieve Operational Attributes?".
* `scope` (string): The set of entries at or below the BaseDN that may be considered potential matches in a search. Console display name: "Scope".
* `sizeLimit` (string): The maximum number of entries to retrieve. The default is 0, which will return all entries. Console display name: "Size Limit".
* `timeLimit` (string): The maximum amount of time allowed for the search in seconds. The default is 10 seconds and the maximum is 30 seconds. Console display name: "Time Limit".
* `typesOnly` (string): Only the attribute names but not values will be returned when this is enabled. Console display name: "Types only".
* `useJsonAttributes` (string): Console display name: "Input attributes as JSON?".


Example:
```terraform
resource "pingone_davinci_connector_instance" "pingOneLDAPConnector" {
  environment_id = var.pingone_environment_id

  connector = {
    id = "pingOneLDAPConnector"
  }
  name = "My awesome pingOneLDAPConnector"
```

## LaunchDarkly API

Connector ID (`connector.id` in the resource): `connector-oai-launchdarklyrestapi`

Properties (used under the `properties` block in the resource as a key in the JSON object):

* `associateRepositoriesAndProjects_associateRepositoriesAndProjectsRequest_AssociateRepositoriesAndProjectsRequest_mappings` (string): Console display name: "Mappings".
* `authApiKey` (string): The authentication key to the LaunchDarkly REST API. Console display name: "API Key".
* `basePath` (string): The base URL for contacting the API. Console display name: "Base Path".
* `copyFeatureFlag_copyFeatureFlagRequest_CopyFeatureFlagRequestSource_currentVersion` (string): Optional flag version. If you include this, the operation only succeeds if the current flag version in the environment matches this version. Console display name: "CurrentVersion".
* `copyFeatureFlag_copyFeatureFlagRequest_CopyFeatureFlagRequestSource_key` (string): The environment key. Console display name: "Key".
* `copyFeatureFlag_copyFeatureFlagRequest_CopyFeatureFlagRequestTarget_currentVersion` (string): Optional flag version. If you include this, the operation only succeeds if the current flag version in the environment matches this version. Console display name: "CurrentVersion".
* `copyFeatureFlag_copyFeatureFlagRequest_CopyFeatureFlagRequestTarget_key` (string): The environment key. Console display name: "Key".
* `copyFeatureFlag_copyFeatureFlagRequest_CopyFeatureFlagRequest_comment` (string): Optional comment. Console display name: "Comment".
* `copyFeatureFlag_copyFeatureFlagRequest_CopyFeatureFlagRequest_excludedActions` (string): Optional list of the flag changes NOT to copy from the source environment to the target environment. You may include either  &lt;code&gt;includedActions&lt;/code&gt; or &lt;code&gt;excludedActions&lt;/code&gt;, but not both. If you include neither, then all flag changes will be copied. Console display name: "ExcludedActions".
* `copyFeatureFlag_copyFeatureFlagRequest_CopyFeatureFlagRequest_includedActions` (string): Optional list of the flag changes to copy from the source environment to the target environment. You may include either &lt;code&gt;includedActions&lt;/code&gt; or &lt;code&gt;excludedActions&lt;/code&gt;, but not both. If you include neither, then all flag changes will be copied. Console display name: "IncludedActions".
* `copyFeatureFlag_feature_flag_key` (string): The feature flag key. The key identifies the flag in your code. Console display name: "FeatureFlagKey".
* `copyFeatureFlag_project_key` (string): The project key. Console display name: "ProjectKey".
* `createBigSegmentExport_environment_key` (string): The environment key. Console display name: "EnvironmentKey".
* `createBigSegmentExport_project_key` (string): The project key. Console display name: "ProjectKey".
* `createBigSegmentExport_segment_key` (string): The segment key. Console display name: "SegmentKey".
* `createBigSegmentImport_environment_key` (string): The environment key. Console display name: "EnvironmentKey".
* `createBigSegmentImport_file` (string): CSV file containing keys. Console display name: "File".
* `createBigSegmentImport_mode` (string): Import mode. Use either `merge` or `replace`. Console display name: "Mode".
* `createBigSegmentImport_project_key` (string): The project key. Console display name: "ProjectKey".
* `createBigSegmentImport_segment_key` (string): The segment key. Console display name: "SegmentKey".
* `createBigSegmentStoreIntegration_createBigSegmentStoreIntegrationRequest_CreateBigSegmentStoreIntegrationRequest_config` (string): The global integration settings, as specified by the &lt;code&gt;formVariables&lt;/code&gt; in the &lt;code&gt;manifest.json&lt;/code&gt; for this integration. Console display name: "Config".
* `createBigSegmentStoreIntegration_createBigSegmentStoreIntegrationRequest_CreateBigSegmentStoreIntegrationRequest_name` (string): Name to identify the integration. Console display name: "Name".
* `createBigSegmentStoreIntegration_createBigSegmentStoreIntegrationRequest_CreateBigSegmentStoreIntegrationRequest_on` (string): Whether the integration configuration is active. Default value is false. Console display name: "On".
* `createBigSegmentStoreIntegration_createBigSegmentStoreIntegrationRequest_CreateBigSegmentStoreIntegrationRequest_tags` (string): Tags to associate with the integration. Console display name: "Tags".
* `createBigSegmentStoreIntegration_environment_key` (string): The environment key. Console display name: "EnvironmentKey".
* `createBigSegmentStoreIntegration_integration_key` (string): The integration key, either `redis` or `dynamodb`. Console display name: "IntegrationKey".
* `createBigSegmentStoreIntegration_project_key` (string): The project key. Console display name: "ProjectKey".
* `createDeploymentEvent_createDeploymentEventRequest_CreateDeploymentEventRequest_applicationKey` (string): The application key. This defines the granularity at which you want to view your insights metrics. Typically it is the name of one of the GitHub repositories that you use in this project.&lt;br/&gt;&lt;br/&gt;LaunchDarkly automatically creates a new application each time you send a unique application key. Console display name: "ApplicationKey".
* `createDeploymentEvent_createDeploymentEventRequest_CreateDeploymentEventRequest_applicationKind` (string): The kind of application. Default: &lt;code&gt;server&lt;/code&gt;. Console display name: "ApplicationKind".
* `createDeploymentEvent_createDeploymentEventRequest_CreateDeploymentEventRequest_applicationName` (string): The application name. This defines how the application is displayed. Console display name: "ApplicationName".
* `createDeploymentEvent_createDeploymentEventRequest_CreateDeploymentEventRequest_deploymentMetadata` (string): A JSON object containing metadata about the deployment. Console display name: "DeploymentMetadata".
* `createDeploymentEvent_createDeploymentEventRequest_CreateDeploymentEventRequest_environmentKey` (string): The environment key. Console display name: "EnvironmentKey".
* `createDeploymentEvent_createDeploymentEventRequest_CreateDeploymentEventRequest_eventMetadata` (string): A JSON object containing metadata about the event. Console display name: "EventMetadata".
* `createDeploymentEvent_createDeploymentEventRequest_CreateDeploymentEventRequest_eventTime` (string): The time, in Unix milliseconds, when the event occurred. If not included, the time will default to when the event is processed and stored in LaunchDarkly. Console display name: "EventTime".
* `createDeploymentEvent_createDeploymentEventRequest_CreateDeploymentEventRequest_eventType` (string): The event type. Console display name: "EventType".
* `createDeploymentEvent_createDeploymentEventRequest_CreateDeploymentEventRequest_projectKey` (string): The project key. Console display name: "ProjectKey".
* `createDeploymentEvent_createDeploymentEventRequest_CreateDeploymentEventRequest_version` (string): The application version. You can set the application version to any string that includes only letters, numbers, periods (&lt;code&gt;.&lt;/code&gt;), hyphens (&lt;code&gt;-&lt;/code&gt;), or underscores (&lt;code&gt;_&lt;/code&gt;).&lt;br/&gt;&lt;br/&gt;We recommend setting the application version to at least the first seven characters of the SHA or to the tag of the GitHub commit for this deployment. Console display name: "Version".
* `createDeploymentEvent_createDeploymentEventRequest_CreateDeploymentEventRequest_versionName` (string): The version name. This defines how the version is displayed. Console display name: "VersionName".
* `createExperiment_createExperimentRequest_CreateExperimentRequestIteration_canReshuffleTraffic` (string): Whether to allow the experiment to reassign traffic to different variations when you increase or decrease the traffic in your experiment audience (true) or keep all traffic assigned to its initial variation (false). Defaults to true. Console display name: "CanReshuffleTraffic".
* `createExperiment_createExperimentRequest_CreateExperimentRequestIteration_flags` (string): Details on the feature flag and targeting rules for this iteration. Console display name: "Flags".
* `createExperiment_createExperimentRequest_CreateExperimentRequestIteration_hypothesis` (string): The expected outcome of this experiment. Console display name: "Hypothesis".
* `createExperiment_createExperimentRequest_CreateExperimentRequestIteration_metrics` (string): Details on the metrics for this experiment. Console display name: "Metrics".

* `getSegments_filter` (string): Accepts filter by kind, query, tags, unbounded, external, or included and excluded segment keys. To filter by kind or query, use the `equals` operator. To filter by tags, use the `anyOf` operator. Query is a 'fuzzy' search across segment key, name, and description. Example: `filter=tags anyOf ['enterprise', 'beta'],query equals 'toggle'` returns segments with 'toggle' in their key, name, or description that also have 'enterprise' or 'beta' as a tag. To filter by unbounded, use the `equals` operator. Example: `filter=unbounded equals true`. To filter by external, use the `exists` operator. Example: `filter=external exists true`. To exclude segments from results, use `filter=excludedKeys anyOf ['segmentKey1', 'segmentKey2']`. Console display name: "Filter".

Example: `sort=name` sort by names ascending or `sort=-name,creationDate` sort by names descending and creationDate ascending. Console display name: "Sort".

## LexisNexis

Connector ID (`connector.id` in the resource): `lexisnexisV2Connector`

Properties (used under the `properties` block in the resource as a key in the JSON object):

* `apiKey` (string): Your LexisNexis API key, such as “o3x9ywfs26rm1zvl”. Console display name: "API Key".
* `apiUrl` (string): The API URL to target. For a custom value, select Use Custom API URL and enter a value in the Custom API URL field. Console display name: "API URL".
* `customAttribute` (string): Define additional parameters to send to LexisNexis, such as user attributes. For a list of valid parameters, see the LexisNexis documentation or speak to a LexisNexis representative. Console display name: "Additional Parameters".
* `customCSS` (string): Customize the CSS for the user-facing interface. Console display name: "CSS".
* `customDeliveryMethod` (string): Select a variable from your flow to dynamically set the OTP method. The value of the variable must be “email”, “sms”, or “voice”. Console display name: "Dynamic Delivery Method".
* `customHTML` (string): Customize the HTML for the user-facing interface. Console display name: "HTML".
* `customProfilingUrl` (string): The URL for the device profiling script, such as “https://h.online-metrix.net/fp/tags.js”. Console display name: "Custom Profiling URL".
* `customRequiredParameter` (string): The key for the required parameter to send to LexisNexis, such as “account_email”. Console display name: "Custom Required Parameter".
* `customScript` (string): Write custom JavaScript. Caution: Custom code is for advanced users only. Before using custom code, review the security risks in the DaVinci documentation by searching for "Using custom code safely". Console display name: "Script".
* `ddpProfilingUrl` (string): The source of the device profiling script. For a custom value, select Use Custom Profiling URL and enter a value in the Custom Profiling URL field. Console display name: "DDP Profiling URL".
* `deliveryMethod` (string): The method to use to deliver the OTP. To change the method dynamically, select Use Dynamic Delivery Method and provide a variable in the Dynamic Delivery Method field. Console display name: "Delivery Method".
* `email` (string): The user's email address, such as “jsmith@example.com”. Console display name: "Email".
* `emailBody` (string): The body of the email message containing the OTP, such as “Your one-time passcode is:${LineBreak}${OTP}${LineBreak}If you did not make this request, contact your administrator.”. The ${ExpirePeriod} variable uses the value from the OTP Timeout field. Console display name: "Email Body".
* `emailTitle` (string): The title of the email message containing the OTP, such as “Your one-time passcode”. Console display name: "Email Title".
* `events_type` (string): Select the LexisNexis event type to use. Console display name: "Event Type".
* `htmlConfig` (string): Console display name: "".
* `htmlConfig1` (string): Console display name: "".
* `loadingText` (string): The message to show when collecting the device profile. Console display name: "Device Profiling Message".
* `orgId` (string): Your LexisNexis organization ID, such as “4en6ll2s”. Console display name: "Organization ID".
* `otpLength` (string): The number of digits in the OTP. Console display name: "OTP Length".
* `otpTimeout` (string): The amount of time in minutes that the OTP is valid. Console display name: "OTP Timeout".
* `phoneNumber` (string): The user's phone number, including country code, such as “1-604-697-7040”. Console display name: "Phone Number".
* `policy` (string): The name of the Dynamic Decision Platform policy to use, such as “OTP”. The policy determines which LexisNexis service is used, such as ThreatMetrix, Emailage, or Phone Finder. You can find the policy names in your LexisNexis portal. Names are case sensitive. Console display name: "Policy".
* `queryType` (string): Select the Query type to use. Console display name: "Query Type".
* `requiredParameter` (string): Select the main parameter to send to LexisNexis, then provide the value in the Required Parameter Value field. You can optionally provide more parameters in Additional Parameters. For a dynamic value, select Use Custom Required Parameter and enter a value in the Custom Required Parameter field. Console display name: "Required Parameter".
* `requiredParameterValue` (string): Enter the value for the Required Parameter, such as "A-123456C". Console display name: "Required Parameter Value".
* `review_status` (string): Select the fallback review status to use when LexisNexis reports that no device profiling session exists. This happens when the device profiling script is blocked or times out. Console display name: "Review Status for Unknown Sessions".
* `service_type` (string): Select the LexisNexis service to use. Console display name: "Service Type".
* `session_id` (string): The unique ID associated with the device profile, provided by the Get Device Profile capability. Console display name: "Session Id".
* `smsMessage` (string): The body of the SMS message containing the OTP, such as “Your one-time passcode is:${LineBreak}${OTP}${LineBreak}If you did not make this request, contact your administrator.”. Limited to 160 ASCII characters. The ${ExpirePeriod} variable uses the value from the OTP Timeout field. Console display name: "SMS Message".
* `timeOut` (string): The maximum amount of time in seconds to allow the device profiling script to run, such as “5”. If you frequently get “unknown session” results from the DDP capability, consider increasing this time. The value must be from 1-30. Console display name: "Timeout".
* `useCustomApiURL` (string): The API URL to target, such as “https://h.online-metrix.net”. Console display name: "Custom API URL".
* `validationRules` (string): Rules to check to validate form inputs. Console display name: "Form Validation Rules".

## Location Policy

Connector ID (`connector.id` in the resource): `locationPolicyConnector`

Properties (used under the `properties` block in the resource as a key in the JSON object):

* `confidenceThreshold` (string): The degree of certainty that the user’s travel between previously seen locales is impossible. Console display name: "".
* `geolocationPermission` (string): The message displayed that asks users for permission to access their location. Console display name: "".
* `ipAddressList` (string): The list of CIDR blocks or IP addresses to allow, such as “131.10.55.1/24”. Separate multiple IP addresses with commas. Console display name: "IP Addresses".
* `regions` (string): The list of countries, regions, and cities to allow, such as "US, GB, Russia, Ontario, Queensland, California, Tokyo, Prague, Guangzhou". Use the English name for countries, regions and cities. For countries, you can also use ISO-3166 Alpha-2 codes. Console display name: "Locations".


Example:
```terraform
resource "pingone_davinci_connector_instance" "locationPolicyConnector" {
  environment_id = var.pingone_environment_id

  connector = {
    id = "locationPolicyConnector"
  }
  name = "My awesome locationPolicyConnector"
  property {
    name  = "confidenceThreshold"
    type  = "string"
    value = var.locationpolicyconnector_property_confidence_threshold
  }
  property {
    name  = "geolocationPermission"
    type  = "string"
    value = var.locationpolicyconnector_property_geolocation_permission
  }

  }

    value = var.locationpolicyconnector_property_regions
  }
}
```


## MFA

Connector ID (`connector.id` in the resource): `mfaUseCaseConnector`

Properties (used under the `properties` block in the resource as a key in the JSON object):

* `activationStatus` (string): The current status of the device. If a device has an ACTIVATION_REQUIRED status, activate it before you add it as a trusted device. Console display name: "Activation Status".
* `applicationId` (string): The unique identifier of the native application which initiated the authentication flow. Console display name: "Application".
* `applicationIds` (string): Select the application(s) that can be used with the push settings. Leave this list empty to allow all available native applications in the environment to be used. Console display name: "Applications".
* `assertion` (string): A string that specifies the authenticator assertion response. The string contains the signed challenge needed to complete the MFA authentication. Console display name: "Assertion".
* `attestation` (string): A read-only string that specifies the public key and signed challenge used to complete registration and device activation. The attestation is generated by the browser as a response to a specific user action, such as a fingerprint scan or tap on a security key. Console display name: "Attestation".
* `authTemplateName` (string): Indicates whether the notification is intended for a user authentication flow. Console display name: "Notification Type".
* `authenticatingApplicationId` (string): The unique identifier for the mobile application used to authenticate a user. Console display name: "Application".
* `clientContext` (string): Additional attributes that can be passed to the mobile application during the authentication. Console display name: "Mobile Client Context".
* `compatibility` (string): Console display name: "WebAuthn Browser Compatibility".
* `customApplicationId` (string): Console display name: "Application ID".
* `customAuthenticatingApplicationId` (string): Console display name: "Application ID".
* `customDeviceAuthenticationPolicyId` (string): Console display name: "MFA Policy ID".
* `customDeviceType` (string): Console display name: "Enter Device Type".
* `customNotificationPolicyId` (string): Console display name: "Notification Policy ID".
* `customTemplateVariant` (string): You can enter a custom template name, or leave blank to use the default template. You can also enter a parameter from a previous connector, or any text. Console display name: "Custom Value".
* `device` (string): The PingOne MFA Device. Console display name: "Device".
* `deviceAuthenRpId` (string): If you define a Relying Party ID (RPID) here, it overrides the RPID defined in the FIDO policy in the PingOne admin console. Console display name: "Relying Party ID".
* `deviceAuthenticationId` (string): The unique identifier for the MFA Device Authentication. Console display name: "Device Authentication ID".
* `deviceAuthenticationPolicyId` (string): The ID of your PingOne MFA device authentication policy. Console display name: "MFA Policy ID".
* `deviceId` (string): The MFA device type unique identifier (UUID) to be used for authentication. If this value is not provided,  Authentication will be as per  MFA policy settings. Console display name: "Device ID".
* `deviceType` (string): The type of device used during authentication. Console display name: "Device Type".
* `devices` (string): The PingOne MFA Devices. Console display name: "Devices".
* `email` (string): The email address to associate with the device. Applies only to devices that use email during authentication. Console display name: "Email".
* `extension` (string): The phone extension for this device. It can include digits, comma, # and *. If there is more than one extension then a comma should separate the extension and the nested extension. Console display name: "Extension".
* `fido2Settings` (boolean): Show advanced fields for FIDO2 Settings. Console display name: "Show advanced fields".
* `fidoCompatibility` (string): A string that specifies the FIDO Authenticators that are allowed to be used. Options are FULL (compatible with FIDO2, platform biometrics, and security key) and NONE (not compatible with FIDO). Console display name: "FIDO Compatibility".
* `mfaEnabled` (boolean): Enable or disable user MFA. Console display name: "Enable User MFA".
* `mfaPolicyId` (string): The ID of your PingOne MFA device authentication policy. Console display name: "MFA Policy Id".
* `mfaSettings` (boolean): Show advanced fields for MFA Settings. Console display name: "Show advanced fields".
* `mobilePayload` (string): A signed challenge generated by PingOne MFA mobile SDK. Console display name: "Mobile Payload".
* `nickname` (string): A nickname that identifies this device. The device nickname is limited to 100 characters. Console display name: "Device Nickname".
* `notificationPolicyId` (string): A unique identifier for the policy. Console display name: "Notification Policy".
* `notificationSettings` (boolean): Show advanced fields for Notification Settings. Console display name: "Show advanced fields".
* `origin` (string): The address of the server sending the initial registration challenge to the device. Console display name: "Origin".
* `otp` (string): The one-time passcode (OTP) sent to the user. Console display name: "One-time Passcode".
* `otpSettings` (boolean): Show advanced fields for OTP Settings. Console display name: "Show advanced fields".
* `pairingKeyId` (string): The unique identifier for the pairing key. Console display name: "Pairing Key ID".
* `phone` (string): The phone number to associate with the device. Applies only to devices that use SMS and Voice SMS messages during authentication. Console display name: "Phone Number".
* `pushSettings` (boolean): Show advanced fields for PUSH Settings. Console display name: "Show advanced fields".
* `reason` (string): The reason that the authentication was canceled. 
Possible values are SIGNOUT, CHANGE_DEVICE, ADD_DEVICE. Any other reason will get the value - DEFAULT. Console display name: "Reason For Cancellation
".
* `rpId` (string): If you define a Relying Party ID (RPID) here, it overrides the RPID defined in the FIDO policy in the PingOne admin console. Console display name: "Relying Party ID".
* `rpName` (string): A string that specifies the relying party's human-readable display name. Console display name: "Relying Party Name".
* `sectionLabelDeviceDetails` (string): Console display name: "Device Details".
* `sectionLabelFido` (string): Console display name: "FIDO2 Settings".
* `sectionLabelMfaSettings` (string): Console display name: "MFA Settings".
* `sectionLabelNotification` (string): Console display name: "Notification Settings".
* `sectionLabelOtp` (string): Console display name: "OTP Settings".
* `sectionLabelPush` (string): Console display name: "Push Settings".
* `sectionLabelUserDetails` (string): Console display name: "User and Device Details".
* `selectedDeviceOtp` (string): The one-time passcode (OTP) of the device used to authenticate. If the Device ID is not provided, the OTP is validated against all the applicable devices. Console display name: "One-time Passcode".
* `serialNumber` (string): The unique identifier for the OATH token. Console display name: "Serial Number".
* `setDeviceOrder` (string): Select how to set the device order. Console display name: "Set Device Order".
* `setFilterFlag` (boolean): Filter devices by activation status and device type. Console display name: "Filters".
* `showAdvancedFields` (boolean): Show advanced fields. Console display name: "Show advanced fields".
* `showPoweredBy` (string): Console display name: "".
* `skipButtonPress` (string): Console display name: "".
* `statusFilter` (string): non-active devices are not usable during an authentication. Console display name: "Status".
* `templateLocale` (string): Add a locale to allow localized notifications for end-users. ISO Language Codes are supported. Console display name: "Notification Locale".
* `templateVariables` (string): If Custom variables are defined in the notification body, map them here. Console display name: "Notification Variables".
* `templateVariant` (string): The name of a custom notification defined in PingOne. If the form you want is not listed, select Enter Custom Value. Console display name: "Notification Name".
* `userAgent` (string): Browser user agent. Console display name: "User Agent".
* `userId` (string): The unique identifier for the user. Console display name: "User ID".
* `yubiKey` (string): The one-time passcode used to authenticate the YubiKey. Console display name: "YubiKey".

## Mailchimp

Connector ID (`connector.id` in the resource): `connectorMailchimp`

Properties (used under the `properties` block in the resource as a key in the JSON object):

* `allowlistEmail` (string): Grants permission to send emails to a specific email address. Console display name: "Allowlist Email".
* `body` (string): The raw custom JSON body. Console display name: "Body".
* `denylistEmail` (string): Add email address to the denylist. Console display name: "Denylist Email".
* `endpoint` (string): Use a Transactional API endpoint, such as /messages/send, /allowlists/add, /rejects/add, etc. Console display name: "Endpoint".
* `headers` (string): Add HTTP headers and provide their values. Console display name: "Headers".
* `messageFromEmail` (string): The from address of the email being sent. Console display name: "From Email".
* `messageSubject` (string): Title of the email being sent. Console display name: "Subject".
* `messageText` (string): Text of the email being sent. Console display name: "Text".
* `messageToEmail` (string): The to address(es) of the email being sent. Console display name: "Recipient Email(s)".
* `method` (string): The HTTP Method. Console display name: "Method".
* `optionalComment` (string): Optional transaction description. Console display name: "Comment".
* `removeAllowlistEmail` (string): Removes desired email from the allowlist. Console display name: "Remove Email".
* `storeId` (string): Unique ID for a store. Console display name: "Store ID".
* `transactionalApiKey` (string): The Transactional API Key is used to send data to the transactional API. Console display name: "Transactional API Key".
* `transactionalApiVersion` (string): Mailchimp - Transactional API Version. Console display name: "Transactional API Version".


Example:
```terraform
resource "pingone_davinci_connector_instance" "connectorMailchimp" {
  environment_id = var.pingone_environment_id

  connector = {
    id = "connectorMailchimp"
  }
  name = "My awesome connectorMailchimp"
  property {
    name  = "allowlistEmail"
    type  = "string"
    value = var.connectormailchimp_property_allowlist_email
  }
  property {
    name  = "body"
    type  = "string"
    value = var.connectormailchimp_property_body
  }
  property {
    name  = "denylistEmail"
    type  = "string"
    value = var.connectormailchimp_property_denylist_email

  property {
    name  = "endpoint"
    type  = "string"
    value = var.connectormailchimp_property_endpoint
  }
  property {
    name  = "headers"
    type  = "string"
    value = var.connectormailchimp_property_headers
  }
  property {
    name  = "messageFromEmail"
    type  = "string"
    value = var.connectormailchimp_property_message_from_email
  }
  property {
    name  = "messageSubject"
    type  = "string"
    value = var.connectormailchimp_property_message_subject
  }
  property {
    name  = "messageText"
    type  = "string"
    value = var.connectormailchimp_property_message_text
  }
  property {
    name  = "messageToEmail"
    type  = "string"
    value = var.connectormailchimp_property_message_to_email
  }
  property {
    name  = "method"
    type  = "string"
    value = var.connectormailchimp_property_method
  }
  property {
    name  = "optionalComment"
    type  = "string"
    value = var.connectormailchimp_property_optional_comment
  }
```

## Mailgun

Connector ID (`connector.id` in the resource): `connectorMailgun`

Properties (used under the `properties` block in the resource as a key in the JSON object):

* `apiKey` (string): Mailgun API Key. Console display name: "API Key".
* `apiVersion` (string): Mailgun API Version. Console display name: "API Version".
* `body` (string): The raw JSON body. Console display name: "Body".
* `domainEvent` (string): The type of domain event to return (see connector documentation for complete list of event types). Console display name: "Domain Event".
* `domainEventDuration` (string): Period of time for the desired event, e.g. 15h, 1d, 2m, etc. (optional). Console display name: "Domain Event Duration".
* `emailBcc` (string): Same as the “To” parameter but for bcc. You can use commas to separate multiple recipients. (optional). Console display name: "BCC".
* `emailCc` (string): Same as the “To” parameter but for cc. You can use commas to separate multiple recipients. (optional). Console display name: "CC".
* `emailSubject` (string): Subject of the email. Console display name: "Subject".
* `emailTag` (string): Tag string. (optional). Console display name: "Tag".
* `emailText` (string): Body of the email. (text version). Console display name: "Message".
* `endpoint` (string): Mailgun API endpoints, e.g. "/lists/MAILING_LIST@email.com/members" etc... Console display name: "Endpoint".
* `fromAddress` (string): Sender email address with the desired domain (e.g. YOU@YOUR_DOMAIN_NAME). Console display name: "From Address".
* `fromName` (string): Name of the sender (e.g. John Smith). Console display name: "Sender Name".
* `headers` (string): Add HTTP headers and provide their values. Console display name: "Headers".
* `mailgunDomain` (string): Name of the desired domain (e.g. mail.mycompany.com). Console display name: "Domain".
* `mailingListAccessLevel` (string): The access level of the mailing list. Either: readonly (default), members, everyone. Console display name: "Access Level".
* `mailingListAddress` (string): A valid email address for the mailing list, e.g. developers@mailgun.com. Console display name: "Mailing List Address".
* `mailingListDescription` (string): A brief description for the mailing list. (optional). Console display name: "Description".
* `mailingListMemberAddress` (string): Valid email address of the new member, e.g. new.member@gmail.com. Console display name: "Member Address".
* `mailingListMemberAttributes` (string): JSON-encoded dictionary string for arbitrary attributes of the specified member. Console display name: "Member Attributes".
* `mailingListMemberName` (string): Name of the member. (optional). Console display name: "Member Name".
* `mailingListMemberSubscriptionStatus` (string): Toggle the switch "on" to add as subscribed, leave the switch "off" to set as unsubscribed. Console display name: "Member Subscription Status".
* `mailingListMemberUpsert` (string): Toggle the switch "on" to enable updating a member if present, leave the switch "off" to raise an error in case of a duplicate member. Console display name: "Member Upsert Permissons".
* `mailingListName` (string): Mailing list name, e.g. Developers. (optional). Console display name: "Name".
* `mailingListReplyPreference` (string): Set where replies should go: “list” (default) or “sender”. (optional). Console display name: "Reply Preference".
* `method` (string): The HTTP Method. Console display name: "Method".
* `newMailingListMemberAddress` (string): New valid email address of the member, e.g. new.member@gmail.com (optional). Console display name: "New Member Address".
* `queryParameters` (string): Add query parameters and provide their values. Console display name: "Query Parameters".
* `toAddress` (string): Email address of the recipient(s). You can use commas to separate multiple recipients. Console display name: "To Address".


Example:

* `v3RESTStatcountersGet_counter_resolution` (string): Mandatory: Defines the timescale of aggregation for your statistics:  - `Highest` (5-minute intervals) - `Hour` - `Day` - `Lifetime`. Console display name: "CounterResolution".
* `v3RESTStatcountersGet_counter_source` (string): Mandatory: Defines the scope of aggregation for your statistics - API Key, campaign, sender email or contact list. Console display name: "CounterSource".
* `v3RESTStatcountersGet_counter_timing` (string): Mandatory: Defines the reference timestamp for aggregation of statistics. For more information go to https://dev.mailjet.com/guides/#event-based-vs-message-based-stats-timing   Note: Event-based stats cannot be retrieved for CounterSource=Sender. Console display name: "CounterTiming".
* `v3RESTStatcountersGet_from_ts` (string): Retrieve statistics for messages sent after the specified timestamp. Mandatory when `CounterResolution` is different from `Lifetime`. Console display name: "FromTs".
* `v3RESTStatcountersGet_source_id` (string): List of either Campaign IDs or ContactsList IDs (separated by commas). Mandatory when `CounterSource` indicates `Campaign` or `List`. Console display name: "SourceID".
* `v3RESTStatcountersGet_to_ts` (string): Retrieve statistics for campaigns sent before the specified timestamp. Console display name: "ToTS".
* `v3RESTStatisticsLinkClickGet_campaign_id` (string): Mandatory: Retrieves statistics only for the specified campaign ID. Console display name: "CampaignID".

## Microsoft Defender for Endpoint

Connector ID (`connector.id` in the resource): `microsoftDefenderConnector`

Properties (used under the `properties` block in the resource as a key in the JSON object):

* `baseUrl` (string): The regional API endpoint for your Microsoft Defender for Endpoint tenant. Select the region where your tenant data is stored. Console display name: "Base URL".
* `clientId` (string): The Application (client) ID assigned to your app registration in the Microsoft Entra admin center. Console display name: "Client ID".
* `clientSecret` (string): The confidential client secret generated for your application to authenticate against the Microsoft identity platform. Console display name: "Client Secret".
* `comment` (string): The comment to associate with the action. Console display name: "Comment".
* `deviceId` (string): The device identifier. Accepts the Microsoft Defender for Endpoint device ID, the Microsoft Entra device ID, or the computer DNS name. Console display name: "Device ID".
* `isolationType` (string): Specifies how the device is isolated from the network. Full isolation blocks all network access except to Defender. Selective isolation allows limited app connectivity. Unmanaged Device targets devices not enrolled in Defender. Console display name: "Isolation Type".
* `tenantId` (string): The unique identifier of your Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD) tenant. Console display name: "Tenant ID".
* `userId` (string): The sAMAccountName or username portion of the identity (e.g., jsmith from jsmith@contoso.com). Console display name: "User ID".


Example:
```terraform
resource "pingone_davinci_connector_instance" "microsoftDefenderConnector" {
  environment_id = var.pingone_environment_id

  connector = {
    id = "microsoftDefenderConnector"
  }
  name = "My awesome microsoftDefenderConnector"
  property {
    name  = "baseUrl"
    type  = "string"
    value = var.microsoftdefenderconnector_property_base_url
  }
  property {
    name  = "clientId"
    type  = "string"
    value = var.microsoftdefenderconnector_property_client_id
  }
  property {
    name  = "clientSecret"
    type  = "string"
    value = var.microsoftdefenderconnector_property_client_secret
  }
  property {
    name  = "comment"
    type  = "string"
    value = var.microsoftdefenderconnector_property_comment
  }
  property {
    name  = "deviceId"
    type  = "string"
    value = var.microsoftdefenderconnector_property_device_id
  }
  property {
    name  = "isolationType"
    type  = "string"
    value = var.microsoftdefenderconnector_property_isolation_type
  }
  property {
    name  = "tenantId"
    type  = "string"
    value = var.microsoftdefenderconnector_property_tenant_id
  }
  property {
    name  = "userId"
    type  = "string"
    value = var.microsoftdefenderconnector_property_user_id
  }
}
```

## Microsoft Dynamics - Customer Insights

Connector ID (`connector.id` in the resource): `microsoftDynamicsCustomerInsightsConnector`

Properties (used under the `properties` block in the resource as a key in the JSON object):

* `baseURL` (string): Base URL. Console display name: "Base URL".
* `body` (string): The raw JSON body, such as "{ "Username": "jsmith@example.com", "ProfileId": "00e8a0000024zkjAAA" }". Console display name: "Body".
* `clientId` (string): Client ID. Console display name: "Client ID".
* `clientSecret` (string): Client Secret. Console display name: "Client Secret".
* `contactEmail` (string): Email address of desired contact. Console display name: "Contact Email".
* `contactFirstName` (string): First name of new contact. Console display name: "First Name".
* `contactId` (string): ID of the desired contact (e.g. 'xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx'). Console display name: "Contact ID".
* `contactLastName` (string): Last name of new contact. Console display name: "Last Name".
* `contactMobile` (string): Mobile phone number of new contact. Console display name: "Phone Number".
* `contactNewEmail` (string): Email address of new contact. Console display name: "Email Address".
* `contactProperties` (string): Additional contact properties (optional). Console display name: "Contact Properties".
* `contactUpdateProperties` (string): Properties that will be updated for an existing contact. Console display name: "Contact Properties".
* `endpoint` (string): Endpoint. Console display name: "Endpoint".
* `environmentName` (string): Environment Name. Console display name: "Environment Name".
* `grantType` (string): Grant Type. Console display name: "Grant Type".
* `headers` (string): Add HTTP headers and provide their values. Console display name: "Headers".
* `leadEmail` (string): Email address of desired lead. Console display name: "Lead Email".

* `leadId` (string): ID of the desired lead (e.g. 'xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx'). Console display name: "Lead ID".
* `leadLastName` (string): Last name of new lead. Console display name: "Last Name".
* `leadMobile` (string): Mobile phone number of new lead. Console display name: "Phone Number".
* `leadNewEmail` (string): Email address of new lead. Console display name: "Email Address".
* `leadProperties` (string): Additional lead properties (optional). Console display name: "Lead Properties".
* `leadUpdateProperties` (string): Properties that will be updated for an existing lead. Console display name: "Lead Properties".
* `method` (string): The HTTP Method. Console display name: "Method".
* `queryParameters` (string): Add query parameters and provide their values. Console display name: "Query Parameters".
* `tenant` (string): Tenant. Console display name: "Tenant".
* `version` (string): Web API Version. Console display name: "Version".

## Microsoft Teams

Connector ID (`connector.id` in the resource): `microsoftTeamsConnector`

Properties (used under the `properties` block in the resource as a key in the JSON object):

* `authType` (string): Console display name: "".
* `bodyData` (string): The body of the API call. Console display name: "Body".
* `button` (string): Console display name: "Microsoft Login".
* `channelId` (string): The ID of the channel to target, such as "0b2b7c5b-4eb2-5c7b-a94b-bea34ac31c30". Console display name: "Channel ID".
* `channels` (string): The channel to target. For a dynamic value, select Use Channel ID and enter a value in the Channel ID field. Console display name: "Channel".
* `chatId` (string): The ID of the chat, such as "19:ce95abaa0e9f4d22a0e0faa6aad76c56@thread.v2". Console display name: "Chat ID".
* `customAuth` (string): Console display name: "".
* `displayName` (string): The display name to assign to the member. Console display name: "Display Name".
* `endpoint` (string): The API endpoint, such as "https://admin.googleapis.com/admin/directory/v1/users/user@example.com". Console display name: "Endpoint".
* `headersForm` (string): Define additional headers to send to Microsoft Teams. For help, see the API documentation. Console display name: "Additional Headers".
* `memberEmail` (string): The email address of the user in the tenant. Console display name: "User Email".
* `memberId` (string): The ID of the member, such as "0b2b7c5b-4eb2-5c7b-a94b-bea34ac31c30". Console display name: "Member ID".
* `members` (string): The member to target. For a dynamic value, select Use Member ID and enter a value in the Member ID field. Console display name: "Member".
* `membershipId` (string): The ID of the membership, such as "MCMjMSMjMDdlYzlhZjItN2NlNS00YWI3LTg2MzgtMTE1NzM2YmJmOTkwIyM5OGMyOGJlZi05OGYxLTQzNWItYTY1OC03MWVlZTE5YzhmNWUjI2U5MTk4MzA3LTRlMzItNDgwMC1hM2M1LTExNTUxYWQ4MzFhMg==". Console display name: "Membership ID".
* `messageBodyData` (string): The JSON object that contains the message body. For help, see "Chat message" in the Microsoft Graph REST API documentation. Console display name: "Message Object".
* `method` (string): The HTTP method of the API call. Console display name: "HTTP Method".
* `paramsForm` (string): Query parameters for the request. Console display name: "Query Parameters".
* `roles` (string): The roles to assign to the member, such as "owner" or "guest". Basic members should not have any assigned roles. Type a role name and press Enter to add it. Console display name: "Roles".
* `showPoweredBy` (string): Console display name: "".
* `skipButtonPress` (string): Console display name: "".
* `teamId` (string): The ID of the team, such as "0b2b7c5b-4eb2-5c7b-a94b-bea34ac31c30". Console display name: "Team ID".
* `teams` (string): The team to target. For a dynamic value, select Use Team ID and enter a value in the Team ID field. Console display name: "Team".
* `userAccessToken` (string): The user’s access token. This token is provided by the Sign on with Microsoft capability. Console display name: "User Access Token".
* `userId` (string): Unique ID of the user or user principal name. Console display name: "User ID".

## Mitek

Connector ID (`connector.id` in the resource): `mitekConnector`

Properties (used under the `properties` block in the resource as a key in the JSON object):

* `clientId` (string): Mitek Client ID. Console display name: "Client ID".
* `clientSecret` (string): Mitek Client Secret. Console display name: "Client Secret".
* `hostURL` (string): The host URL of the Mitek API (do not include `https://`). Console display name: "Mitek Host URL".
* `mitekAttachmentNames` (string): Comma-delimited attachment keys (no spaces), e.g. doc1,doc2. Console display name: "Attachment Keys".
* `mitekDocumentTypes` (string): Select which document types to include. Console display name: "Document Types".
* `mitekEmail` (string): Recipient’s email for the invite. Console display name: "Email".
* `mitekEndDate` (string): Hard cut-off for the request in YYYY-MM-DD format. If not set, Mitek’s default end date is used. Console display name: "End Date".
* `mitekEnvironment` (string): Case-sensitive environment (e.g., 'live'). Defaults to 'live' if left blank. Console display name: "Mitek Environment".
* `mitekLanguage` (string): If undefined, Mitek defaults to English. Console display name: "Language".
* `mitekName` (string): Full legal name as on passport/driver’s license. Middle names not required. Must be at least 2 words. Console display name: "Name".
* `mitekNote` (string): Welcome message shown on the first page of the journey. Overrides the default message configured in the Mitek portal. Console display name: "Note".
* `mitekPhone` (string): Recipient’s mobile number. Must include the country zone and start with either '+' or '00'. Console display name: "Phone".
* `mitekReference` (string): Your unique ID to correlate results (alphanumeric and dashes). Auto-generated if left blank. Console display name: "Reference".
* `mitekScopeAttachments` (string): Include attachments in the scope. Console display name: "Attachments".
* `mitekScopeDocuments` (string): Include documents in the scope. Console display name: "Documents".
* `mitekScopeSelfie` (string): Includes the selfie step in the verification journey. Console display name: "Selfie Capture".
* `mitekSendChoice` (string): Select how to deliver the verification link, either by email or SMS. Console display name: "Send Choice".
* `mitekTabsOrder` (string): Comma-delimited list (no spaces). If not set, the tabs order is derived from the configured scopes. Console display name: "Tabs Order".
* `mitekUseDefaults` (string): Uses your Mitek environment’s configured defaults when no custom scope is provided. Console display name: "Use Defaults".
* `requstAPIVersion` (string): Mitek Request API Version. Console display name: "Request API Version".
* `skWebhookUri` (string): Console display name: "Redirect Webhook URI".

* `showPoweredBy` (string): Console display name: "Show "Powered by" Message".
* `skipButtonPress` (string): Console display name: "Skip Button Press".

```terraform
resource "pingone_davinci_connector_instance" "pingFederateConnectorV2" {
  environment_id = var.pingone_environment_id

  connector = {
    id = "pingFederateConnectorV2"
  }
  name = "My awesome pingFederateConnectorV2"
  property {
    name  = "authType"
    type  = "string"
    value = var.pingfederateconnectorv2_property_auth_type
  }
  property {
    name  = "button"
    type  = "string"
    value = var.pingfederateconnectorv2_property_button
  }
  property {
    name  = "customCSS"
    type  = "string"
    value = var.pingfederateconnectorv2_property_custom_css
  }
  property {
```
