## PingOne Authorize

Connector ID (`connector.id` in the resource): `pingOneAuthorizeConnector`

Properties (used under the `properties` block in the resource as a key in the JSON object):

* `clientId` (string): The Client ID of the PingOne worker application. Console display name: "Client ID".
* `clientSecret` (string): The Client Secret of the PingOne worker application. Console display name: "Client Secret".
* `code` (string): The advice code from a PingOne Authorize policy rule to search for in an array of statements from a decision response. Console display name: "Statement Code".
* `endpointURL` (string): The PingOne Authorize decision endpoint or ID to which the connector submits decision requests. Console display name: "Endpoint".
* `parameters` (string): Input parameters for the decision request. Console display name: "Parameters".
* `statements` (string): The array of statements to search through in a decision response. Console display name: "Statements".
* `userId` (string): The ID of the PingOne user on whose behalf the connector is making a decision request. Console display name: "User ID".


Example:
```terraform
resource "pingone_davinci_connector_instance" "pingOneAuthorizeConnector" {
  environment_id = var.pingone_environment_id

  connector = {
    id = "pingOneAuthorizeConnector"
  }
  name = "My awesome pingOneAuthorizeConnector"
  property {
    name  = "clientId"
    type  = "string"
    value = var.pingoneauthorizeconnector_property_client_id
  }
  property {
    name  = "clientSecret"
    type  = "string"
    value = var.pingoneauthorizeconnector_property_client_secret
  }
  property {
    name  = "code"
    type  = "string"
    value = var.pingoneauthorizeconnector_property_code
  }
  property {
    name  = "endpointURL"
    type  = "string"
    value = var.endpoint_url
  }
  property {
    name  = "parameters"
    type  = "string"
    value = var.pingoneauthorizeconnector_property_parameters
  }
  property {
    name  = "statements"
    type  = "string"
    value = var.pingoneauthorizeconnector_property_statements
  }
  property {
    name  = "userId"
    type  = "string"
    value = var.pingoneauthorizeconnector_property_user_id
  }
}
```

* `serviceUrl` (string): The full URL of the authorization policy provider. Console display name: "Service URL".

## PingOne Credentials

Connector ID (`connector.id` in the resource): `pingOneCredentialsConnector`

Properties (used under the `properties` block in the resource as a key in the JSON object):

* `applicationInstance` (string): Application Instance Id. Console display name: "Application Instance".
* `applyIssue` (string): Array of one or more user IDs for which credentials should be issued. Console display name: "Apply Issue for User ID(s)".
* `applyRevoke` (string): Array of one or more identifiers (UUIDs) of users whose credentials are in a revoke action state and should be revoked. Console display name: "Apply Revoke for User ID(s)".
* `applyUpdate` (string): Array of one or more identifiers (UUIDs) of users whose credentials are in an update action state and should be updated. Console display name: "Apply Update for User ID(s)".
* `clientId` (string): The Client ID of your PingOne Worker application. Console display name: "Client ID".
* `clientSecret` (string): The Client Secret of your PingOne Worker application. Console display name: "Client Secret".
* `credentialId` (string): Identifier (UUID) of the provisioned user credential. Console display name: "Credential ID".
* `credentialTypeId` (string): Identifier (UUID) associated with the credential type. Console display name: "Credential Type ID".
* `credentialsVerificationId` (string): Identifier (UUID) of the verification credential data. Console display name: "Credential Verification ID".
* `didMethod` (string): DID Method. Console display name: "didMethod".
* `digitalWalletApplicationId` (string): Identifier (UUID) associated with the credential digital wallet app. Console display name: "Digital Wallet Application ID".
* `digitalWalletId` (string): Identifier (UUID) of the digital wallet associated with the provisioned credential. Console display name: "Digital Wallet ID".
* `digitalWalletStatus` (string): Status of the wallet. Console display name: "Status".
* `envId` (string): Your PingOne Environment ID. Console display name: "Environment ID".
* `expirationDate` (string): Expiration Date. Console display name: "Expiration Date".
* `issuanceRuleId` (string): Identifier (UUID) of the credential issuance rule. Console display name: "Issuance Rule ID".
* `issuerFilterDids` (string): Array of unique decentralized identifiers (DIDs) to be searched for the Issuer of the presented credential (OPENID4VP only). Console display name: "Filter by DIDs".
* `issuerFilterEnvIds` (string): Array of PingOne environment IDs to be searched for the Issuer of the presented credential. Console display name: "Filter by PingOne Environment ID".
* `message` (string): A message shown to the user by the compatible wallet app to alert the user. Console display name: "Message".
* `notificationMethods` (string): Console display name: "Notification Methods".
* `protocol` (string): Protocol to use for verification; can be OPENID4VP or NATIVE. Defaults to NATIVE. Console display name: "Protocol".
* `region` (string): The region your PingOne environment is in. Console display name: "Region".
* `reqCredType` (string): The ID of the credential type to be verified. Console display name: "Credential Type".
* `requestedCredKeys` (string): Array of strings that identify the key names for selective disclosure to return from the credential. Console display name: "Requested Credential Keys".
* `requestedCredentials` (string): Requested Credentials. Variable Name =>credential type, value=>(comma separated keys). Console display name: "Requested Credentials".
* `showPoweredBy` (string): Console display name: "".
* `skipButtonPress` (string): Console display name: "".
* `templateLocale` (string): Add a locale to allow localized notifications for end-users. ISO Language Codes are supported. Console display name: "Notification Locale".
* `templateVariables` (string): If Custom variables are defined in the notification body, map them here. Console display name: "Notification Variables".
* `templateVariant` (string): You can enter a custom template name, or leave blank to use the default template. You can also enter a parameter from a previous connector, or any text. Console display name: "Custom Value".
* `userId` (string): PingOne user ID. Console display name: "User ID".

## PingOne MFA

Connector ID (`connector.id` in the resource): `pingOneMfaConnector`

Properties (used under the `properties` block in the resource as a key in the JSON object):

* `applicationId` (string): The unique identifier of the native application which initiated the authentication flow. Console display name: "Application".
* `applicationIds` (string): Select the application(s) that can be used with this pairing key. Leave this list empty to allow all available native applications in the environment to be used. Console display name: "Applications".
* `applicationName` (string): The name of the application being authenticated. Console display name: "Application Name".
* `assertion` (string): A string that specifies the authenticator assertion response. The string contains the signed challenge needed to complete the MFA authentication. Console display name: "Assertion".
* `attestation` (string): A read-only string that specifies the public key and signed challenge used to complete registration and device activation. The attestation is generated by the browser as a response to a specific user action, such as a fingerprint scan or tap on a security key. Console display name: "Attestation".
* `authTemplateName` (string): Indicates whether the notification is intended for a user authentication flow or a device authorization flow. Console display name: "Notification Type".
* `authenticatingApplicationId` (string): The unique identifier for the mobile application used to authenticate a user. Console display name: "Application".
* `authenticationCodeId` (string): The unique identifier for the authentication code. Console display name: "Authentication Code ID".
* `clientContext` (string): Additional attributes that can be passed to the mobile application during the authentication. Console display name: "Mobile Client Context".
* `clientId` (string): The Client ID of your PingOne Worker application. Console display name: "Client ID".
* `clientSecret` (string): The Client Secret of your PingOne Worker application. Console display name: "Client Secret".
* `compatibility` (string): Console display name: "WebAuthn Browser Compatibility".
* `createDeviceTestMode` (string): Create device for test purposes only. Console display name: "Test Mode".
* `customApplicationId` (string): Console display name: "Application ID".
* `customAuthenticatingApplicationId` (string): Console display name: "Application ID".
* `customDeviceAuthenticationPolicyId` (string): Console display name: "Device Authentication Policy ID".
* `customDeviceType` (string): Console display name: "Enter Device Type".
* `customNotificationPolicyId` (string): Console display name: "Notification Policy ID".
* `customTemplateVariant` (string): You can enter a custom template name, or leave blank to use the default template. You can also enter a parameter from a previous connector, or any text. Console display name: "Custom Value".
* `defaultDeviceId` (string): Enter the device ID of the device which should be set as the default device. Console display name: "Device ID".
* `device` (string): The PingOne MFA Device. Console display name: "Device".
* `deviceAuthenRpId` (string): If you define a Relying Party ID (RPID) here, it overrides the RPID defined in the FIDO policy in the PingOne admin console. Console display name: "Relying Party ID".
* `deviceAuthenticationId` (string): The unique identifier for the MFA Device Authentication. Console display name: "Device Authentication ID".
* `deviceAuthenticationPolicyId` (string): A unique identifier for the policy. Console display name: "Device Authentication Policy".
* `deviceId` (string): The unique identifier for the MFA device. Console display name: "Device ID".
* `deviceOrderList` (string): Enter the device IDs in the order that the devices should be listed for the user. Console display name: "Set Device Order".
* `deviceType` (string): The type of device used during authentication. Console display name: "Device Type".
* `deviceTypes` (string): Console display name: "Device Types".
* `devices` (string): The PingOne MFA Devices. Console display name: "Devices".
* `duration` (string): The period of time that the authentication code is valid, which can be anywhere from 10 seconds to 30 minutes. Console display name: "Duration".
* `email` (string): The email address to associate with the device. Applies only to devices that use email during authentication. Console display name: "Email".
* `envId` (string): Your PingOne Environment ID. Console display name: "Environment ID".
* `extension` (string): The phone extension for this device. It can include digits, comma, # and *. If there is more than one extension then a comma should separate the extension and the nested extension. Console display name: "Extension".
* `fidoCompatibility` (string): A string that specifies the FIDO Authenticators that are allowed to be used. Options are FULL (compatible with FIDO2, platform biometrics, and security key) and NONE (not compatible with FIDO). Console display name: "FIDO Compatibility".
* `ip` (string): The IP address of the user who initiated the flow. Console display name: "IP".
* `jsonAttributes` (string): An array of objects that determines the explicit order of a user's devices. The first device listed becomes the default device. This property is used as a body parameter to set the order of existing devices. Console display name: "Attributes".
* `lastAuthenticationMethod` (string): Check if the last authentication method used to remember the accessing device matches an allowed authentication method in the current MFA policy being used. Console display name: "Check Last Authentication Method".
* `lastMFATransaction` (string): Details of the last Multi-factor authentication (MFA) transaction. Console display name: "Last MFA transaction".
* `mfaEnabled` (boolean): Enable or disable user MFA. Console display name: "Enable User MFA".
* `mfaPolicyId` (string): The ID of your PingOne MFA device authentication policy. Console display name: "MFA Policy ID".
* `mobilePayload` (string): A signed challenge generated by PingOne MFA mobile SDK. Console display name: "Mobile Payload".
* `nickname` (string): A nickname that identifies this device. The device nickname is limited to 100 characters. Console display name: "Device Nickname".
* `notificationPolicyId` (string): A unique identifier for the policy. Console display name: "Notification Policy".
* `oathResync` (boolean): Indicates if OATH token resync is permitted during registration. Console display name: "OATH Token Resync".
* `oneTimeDeviceTestMode` (string): Create device for test purposes only. Console display name: "Test Mode".
* `oneTimeDeviceType` (string): The one-time device type. Console display name: "Device Type".
* `oneTimeEmailDevice` (string): The email address to associate with the one-time device. Console display name: "Email".
* `oneTimeSmsDevice` (string): The phone number to associate with the one-time SMS device. Console display name: "SMS Phone Number".
* `oneTimeVoiceDevice` (string): The phone number to associate with the one-time Voice device. Console display name: "Voice Phone Number".
* `origin` (string): The address of the server sending the initial registration challenge to the device. Console display name: "Origin".
* `otp` (string): The one-time passcode (OTP) sent to the user. Console display name: "One-time Passcode".
* `pairingKeyId` (string): The unique identifier for the pairing key. Console display name: "Pairing Key ID".
* `phone` (string): The phone number to associate with the device. Applies only to devices that use SMS and Voice SMS messages during authentication. Console display name: "Phone Number".
* `policyFactsApplicationId` (string): The ID of the application being authenticated. Console display name: "Application Id".
* `policyFactsApplicationName` (string): The name of the application being authenticated. Console display name: "Application Name".
* `policyFactsGroups` (json): The groups that the user is part of. Console display name: "User Groups".
* `policyFactsIp` (string): The IP of the requesting device. Console display name: "IP".
* `policyFactsRiskLevel` (string): The Risk Level score that is received from the Risk management service. Console display name: "Risk Level".
* `policyFactsUserAgent` (string): The requesting device’s user agent. Console display name: "User Agent".
* `policyId` (string): The ID of your PingOne MFA device authentication policy. Console display name: "Policy ID".
* `policyRecentAuthMethod` (string): The authentication method used for the most recent transaction. Console display name: "Last transaction authentication method".
* `policyRecentAuthTimestamp` (string): The time at which the most recent transaction occurred. Console display name: "Last transaction time".
* `policyRecentIp` (string): The IP address of the most recent transaction. Console display name: "Last transaction IP".
* `policyRecentPingOneCookie` (string): Enter the last sign-on section from the PingOne Cookie. Console display name: "Last sign-on details".
* `reason` (string): The reason that the authentication was canceled. 
Possible values are SIGNOUT, CHANGE_DEVICE, ADD_DEVICE. Any other reason will get the value - DEFAULT. Console display name: "Reason For Cancellation
".
* `region` (string): The region in which your PingOne environment exists. Console display name: "Region".
* `rememberMeCookie` (string): The cookie that was generated when the remembered device was created. Console display name: "Cookie".
* `rememberMeDeviceType` (string): Console display name: "Device Type".
* `rememberMePayload` (string): Identify the device via a unique device ID combined with a digital signature that ensures information collected about the device has not been tampered with. Console display name: "Payload".
* `rpId` (string): If you define a Relying Party ID (RPID) here, it overrides the RPID defined in the FIDO policy in the PingOne admin console. Console display name: "Relying Party ID".
* `rpName` (string): A string that specifies the relying party's human-readable display name. Console display name: "Relying Party Name".
* `selectedDevice` (string): Indicates whether to use the user's default authentication method or to provide a specific authentication method. Console display name: "Device Details".
* `selectedDeviceId` (string): The selected device id. Console display name: "Device ID".
* `selectedDeviceOtp` (string): The one-time passcode (OTP) of the device used to authenticate. If the Device ID is not provided, the OTP is validated against all the applicable devices. Console display name: "One-time Passcode".
* `serialNumber` (string): The unique identifier for the OAuth token. Console display name: "Serial Number".
* `sessionId` (string): The active PingOne session for the user. Console display name: "Session ID".
* `setDeviceOrder` (string): Select how to set the device order. Console display name: "Set Device Order".
* `setFilterFlag` (boolean): Filter devices by activation status and device type. Console display name: "Filters".
* `showPoweredBy` (string): Console display name: "".
* `skipButtonPress` (string): Console display name: "".
* `status` (string): The current status of the device. If a device has an ACTIVATION_REQUIRED status, activate it before you add it as a trusted device. Console display name: "Activation Status".
* `statusFilter` (string): non-active devices are not usable during an authentication. Console display name: "Status".
* `templateLocale` (string): Add a locale to allow localized notifications for end-users. ISO Language Codes are supported. Console display name: "Notification Locale".
* `templateVariables` (string): If Custom variables are defined in the notification body, map them here. Console display name: "Notification Variables".
* `templateVariant` (string): The name of a custom notification defined in PingOne. If the form you want is not listed, select Enter Custom Value. Console display name: "Notification Name".
* `timeUnit` (string): The units of time used to indicate the authentication code duration. Console display name: "Time Unit".
* `useDeviceOrderJsonAttributes` (string): Console display name: "Input attributes as JSON?".
* `userAgent` (string): Browser user agent. Console display name: "User Agent".
* `userApproval` (string): Specify whether the user will need to approve the authentication after they scan the authentication code using a mobile application. Console display name: "User Approval".
* `userId` (string): The unique identifier for the user. Console display name: "User ID".
* `usernameless` (boolean): Indicates whether the user id is required or obtained from the authentication method used. Console display name: "User ID Not Required".
* `webAuthnChallenge` (string): Applicable for FIDO2 authentication requests. Specify a custom challenge that will replace the automatically generated challenge sent with the authentication request. Must be a valid Base64URL string that decodes to at least 32 bytes of data array. Console display name: "Custom FIDO2 Challenge".
* `webAuthnChallengeForPairing` (string): Applicable for FIDO2 pairing requests. Specify a custom challenge that will replace the automatically generated challenge sent with the pairing request. Must be a valid Base64URL string that decodes to at least 32 bytes of data array. Console display name: "Custom FIDO2 Challenge".
* `workforceDeviceType` (string): The type of device used during authentication. Supported values are: SMS, EMAIL, VOICE, TOTP, YUBIKEY, OATH_TOKEN, PLATFORM, SECURITY_KEY, FIDO2, PINGID_DESKTOP_GEN2. Console display name: "Device Type".
* `workforceDeviceTypes` (string): Console display name: "Device Types".
* `workforcePolicyMfaPolicyId` (string): The ID of the PingID policy evaluation. Console display name: "MFA Policy ID".
* `yubiKey` (string): The one-time passcode used to authenticate the YubiKey. Console display name: "YubiKey".

## PingOne Notifications

Connector ID (`connector.id` in the resource): `notificationsConnector`

Properties (used under the `properties` block in the resource as a key in the JSON object):

* `clientId` (string): The Client ID of your PingOne Worker application. Console display name: "Client ID".
* `clientSecret` (string): The Client Secret of your PingOne Worker application. Console display name: "Client Secret".
* `customTemplateVariant` (string): You can enter a custom template name, or leave blank to use the default template. You can also enter a parameter from a previous connector, or any text. Console display name: "Custom Value".
* `email` (string): The email address to which notifications are sent. Console display name: "Email".
* `envId` (string): Your PingOne Environment ID. Console display name: "Environment ID".
* `notificationPolicyId` (string): A unique identifier for the policy. Console display name: "Notification Policy ID".
* `phone` (string): The phone number to which notifications are sent. Console display name: "Phone Number".
* `region` (string): The region in which your PingOne environment exists. Console display name: "Region".
* `sendSync` (boolean): Indicates whether the connector should wait for the notification vendor to respond to the message request. Console display name: "Wait For Vendor Response".
* `showPoweredBy` (string): Console display name: "".
* `skipButtonPress` (string): Console display name: "".
* `templateLocale` (string): Add a locale to allow localized notifications for end-users. ISO Language Codes are supported. Console display name: "Notification Locale".
* `templateVariables` (string): If custom variables are defined in the notification body, map them here. Console display name: "Notification Variables".
* `templateVariant` (string): The name of a custom notification defined in PingOne. If the form you want is not listed, select Enter Custom Value. Console display name: "Notification Name".
* `userAgent` (string): Browser user agent. Console display name: "User Agent".
* `userId` (string): The unique identifier for the user. Console display name: "User ID".


Example:
```terraform
resource "pingone_davinci_connector_instance" "notificationsConnector" {
  environment_id = var.pingone_environment_id

  connector = {
    id = "notificationsConnector"
  }
  name = "My awesome notificationsConnector"
  property {
    name  = "clientId"
    type  = "string"
    value = var.notificationsconnector_property_client_id
  }
  property {
    name  = "clientSecret"
    type  = "string"
    value = var.notificationsconnector_property_client_secret
  }
  property {
    name  = "customTemplateVariant"
    type  = "string"
    value = var.notificationsconnector_property_custom_template_variant
  }
  property {
    name  = "email"
    type  = "string"
    value = var.notificationsconnector_property_email
  }
  property {
    name  = "envId"
    type  = "string"
    value = var.notificationsconnector_property_env_id
  }
  property {
    name  = "notificationPolicyId"
    type  = "string"
    value = var.notificationsconnector_property_notification_policy_id
  }
  property {
    name  = "phone"
    type  = "string"
    value = var.notificationsconnector_property_phone
  }
  property {
    name  = "region"
    type  = "string"
    value = var.notificationsconnector_property_region
  }
  property {
    name  = "sendSync"
    type  = "boolean"
    value = var.notificationsconnector_property_send_sync
  }
  property {
    name  = "showPoweredBy"
    type  = "string"
    value = var.notificationsconnector_property_show_powered_by
  }
  property {
    name  = "skipButtonPress"
    type  = "string"
    value = var.notificationsconnector_property_skip_button_press
  }
  property {
    name  = "templateLocale"
    type  = "string"
    value = var.notificationsconnector_property_template_locale
  }
  property {
    name  = "templateVariables"
    type  = "string"
    value = var.notificationsconnector_property_template_variables
  }

## PingOne Protect

Connector ID (`connector.id` in the resource): `pingOneRiskConnector`

Properties (used under the `properties` block in the resource as a key in the JSON object):

* `clientId` (string): The id for your Application found in Ping's Dashboard. Console display name: "Client ID".
* `clientSecret` (string): Client Secret from your App in Ping's Dashboard. Console display name: "Client Secret".
* `completionStatus` (string): status of the Risk Evaluation. Console display name: "Risk Evaluation status".
* `cookie` (string): The cookie of the browser/device that triggered the flow. Console display name: "Cookie".
* `createdAt` (string): Date and time the risk evaluation was originally created. Improves processing efficiency. Console display name: "Risk Evaluation Date (Optional)".
* `customAttributes` (string): Your Custom Atributes defined at Ping. Console display name: "Custom Attributes".
* `envId` (string): Your Environment ID provided by Ping. Console display name: "Environment ID".
* `externalId` (string): A unique device identifier generated and managed independently of the Signals SDK (SKrisk). Console display name: "External ID".
* `feedbackCategory` (string): The type of feedback to submit for the risk evaluation. Console display name: "Feedback Category".
* `flowType` (string): The type of flow in which risk is evaluated. Console display name: "Flow Type".
* `ipAddress` (string): The IP address of the user who initiated the flow. Console display name: "IP".
* `password` (string): The password entered by the user. Console display name: "Password".
* `passwordAlgorithm` (string): Password hashing method. Console display name: "Password Hash Algorithm".
* `reason` (string): Optional reason that further explains the feedback. Console display name: "Reason".
* `reasonAutomatedAttack` (string): Reason for AUTOMATED_ATTACK. Console display name: "Reason".
* `reasonCompromisedAccount` (string): Reason for COMPROMISED_ACCOUNT. Console display name: "Reason".
* `reasonFalseHighRisk` (string): Reason for FALSE_HIGH_RISK. Console display name: "Reason".
* `reasonFriendlyBot` (string): Reason for FRIENDLY_BOT. Console display name: "Reason".
* `reasonNewAccountFraud` (string): Reason for NEW_ACCOUNT_FRAUD. Console display name: "Reason".
* `region` (string): The region your PingOne environment is in. Console display name: "Region".
* `riskEvaluationId` (string): The ID of the risk evaluation you are providing feedback on. Console display name: "Risk Evaluation ID".
* `riskId` (string): ID of the Risk Evaluation. Console display name: "Risk Evaluation ID".
* `riskPolicySetId` (string): The risk policy set used during risk evaluation. Console display name: "Risk Policy ID".
* `sessionId` (string): The unique session ID associated with the event. Console display name: "Session ID".
* `showPoweredBy` (string): Console display name: "".
* `skRiskFP` (string): Console display name: "Risk input from device".
* `skipButtonPress` (string): Console display name: "".
* `subtype` (string): The subtype of the flow. Console display name: "Flow Subtype".
* `targetResourceId` (string): The ID for the application or resource the user wants to access. Console display name: "Application ID".
* `targetResourceName` (string): The name of the application or resource the user wants to access. Console display name: "Application Name".
* `targetedPolicy` (boolean): Determines whether the evaluation should automatically select an appropriate policy based on its intended targets, or if a specific policy must be explicitly defined by the user. Console display name: "Targeted Policies Evaluation".
* `userAgent` (string): The user agent of the browser/device that triggered the flow. Console display name: "User Agent".
* `userEmail` (string): The email address of the user whose risk is being evaluated. Console display name: "User Email".
* `userGroups` (string): User groups names. Console display name: "User Groups".
* `userId` (string): The ID of the user whose risk is being evaluated. Console display name: "User ID".
* `userName` (string): The username of the user whose risk is being evaluated. Console display name: "User Name".
* `userPhone` (string): The phone number of the user whose risk is being evaluated. Console display name: "User Phone".
* `userType` (string): Indicates whether the user exists in the PingOne directory or in an external directory. Console display name: "User Type".

## PingOne Scope Consent

Connector ID (`connector.id` in the resource): `pingOneScopeConsentConnector`

Properties (used under the `properties` block in the resource as a key in the JSON object):

* `appConsentHtmlConfig` (string): Console display name: "".
* `applicationConsentScopes` (string): Scopes define the user information that the application wants to access and the user will need to consent to allowing, such as the user’s name, email address, and phone number. You must provide at least one scope. You may provide multiple scopes, each separated by a space. Console display name: "Scopes".
* `applicationIdentifier` (string): Enter the application ID or name of the application you want to locate. Console display name: "Application Identifier".
* `applicationIdentifierIDForAppConsent` (string): Enter the unique identifier of the application that will be used to check, prompt and store consent for the user. Console display name: "Application Identifier".
* `applicationIdentifierNameForAppConsent` (string): Enter the name of the application that will be used to check, prompt and store consent for the user. Console display name: "Application Name".
* `clientId` (string): The Client ID of your PingOne Worker application. Console display name: "Client ID".
* `clientSecret` (string): The Client Secret of your PingOne Worker application. Console display name: "Client Secret".
* `consentIdentifier` (string): A unique identifier for the consent record. Console display name: "Consent Identifier".
* `consentResult` (string): The accept or decline consent result from the user and indicated by "true", “false, “yes”, “no”, "accepted", or "declined". Console display name: "Consent Result".
* `envId` (string): Your PingOne Environment ID. Console display name: "Environment ID".
* `matchApplicationAttribute` (string): Select the application attribute that you want to use to locate an application. Console display name: "Application Attribute".
* `matchApplicationAttributeForAppConsent` (string): Select the application or specify an application identifier that will be used to check, prompt and store consent for the user. Console display name: "Application Attribute".
* `matchConsentAttribute` (string): Enter the consent ID, application ID, or application name of the consent record you want to locate. Console display name: "Consent Attribute".
* `matchUserAttribute` (string): Select the attribute you want to use to locate a user. Console display name: "User Attribute".
* `promptConsent` (string): Indicates whether the user will always be prompted to consent to the application’s request. If disabled, users will only be prompted to consent to these requests if they have not already done so. Console display name: "Always Prompt for Consent".
* `region` (string): The region in which your PingOne environment exists. Console display name: "Region".
* `scopes` (string): Enter the space-separated list of scopes that have been requested. These scopes are validated against the allowed scopes assigned to the PingOne application. Console display name: "Scopes".
* `scopesUnconditional` (string): Enter the space-separated list of scopes that have been requested. These scopes are validated against the allowed scopes assigned to the PingOne application. Console display name: "Scopes".
* `scopesUnconditionalRequired` (string): Enter the space-separated list of scopes that have been requested. These scopes are validated against the allowed scopes assigned to the PingOne application. Console display name: "Scopes".
* `userIdentifier` (string): Enter the user ID, username, or email address of the user you want to locate. Console display name: "User Identifier".

## PingOne Verify

Connector ID (`connector.id` in the resource): `pingOneVerifyConnector`

Properties (used under the `properties` block in the resource as a key in the JSON object):

* `aspectHeight` (number): Height of the aspect ratio. Console display name: "Aspect Height".
* `aspectWidth` (number): Width of the aspect ratio. Console display name: "Aspect Width".
* `attempt` (string): Limit the number verified attempts. Valid values (ALL, LATEST, 1, 2, 3, 4). Console display name: "attempt".
* `biographic` (string): Use this section to add biographic fields. Console display name: "Biographic Fields".
* `challenge` (string): Optional challenge. If not provided, a random challenge will be generated. Console display name: "Challenge".
* `challengeId` (string): Required challenge. To be added to the output for polling in subsequent step. Console display name: "Challenge".
* `clientId` (string): The Client ID of your PingOne Worker application. Console display name: "Client ID".
* `clientSecret` (string): The Client Secret of your PingOne Worker application. Console display name: "Client Secret".
* `colorPicker` (string): Select color. Console display name: "colorPicker".
* `deviceOsType` (string): The OS type of the device to receive SMS messages during verification. Console display name: "Device OS Type".
* `documentId` (string): ID of the data collected from user. Console display name: "Document ID".
* `documentTypeName` (string): Type of the data collected. The document types accepted are determined by the transaction's policy requirements. Console display name: "Document Type".
* `documentTypes` (string): Types of the data collected. The document types accepted are determined by the transaction's policy requirements. Console display name: "Document Types".
* `documentValue` (string): Base64 encoded jpeg or textual data collected from user. Console display name: "Document Value".
* `envId` (string): Your PingOne Environment ID. Console display name: "Environment ID".
* `isLastClientStep` (string): If isLastClientStep is false, the continueLink will be generated and added to the output, otherwise the link will not be added. Console display name: "Is Last Client Step".
* `limit` (number): Number of transactions to return. Console display name: "limit".
* `metadataType` (string): Type of the metadata. Select ALL to get all metadata. Console display name: "Metadata Type".
* `notifyEmail` (string): The email address to receive email notifications during verification. Console display name: "Notification Email Address".
* `notifyPhone` (string): The phone number to receive SMS notifications during verification. Console display name: "Notification Phone Number".
* `probeBiographic` (string): Use this section to add probe biographic fields. Console display name: "Probe Biographic Fields".
* `redirectMessage` (string): Displayed after document collection and before redirecting to the specified URL. Requires a configured Redirect URL. Limited to 256 characters. Console display name: "Redirect Message".
* `redirectUrl` (string): The Redirect URL where the user is returned to after document collection. Only secure (https://) URLs are allowed. Console display name: "Redirect URL".
* `referenceImage` (string): Base64 encoded reference image for facial-comparison-only verify policy. Console display name: "Reference Image".
* `region` (string): The region your PingOne environment is in. Console display name: "Region".
* `selfieId` (string): ID of the selfie. Console display name: "Selfie ID".
* `showPoweredBy` (string): Console display name: "".
* `skipButtonPress` (string): Console display name: "".
* `transactionId` (string): ID of the transaction. Console display name: "Transaction ID".
* `userId` (string): ID of the user. Console display name: "User ID".
* `verifiedType` (string): Selected Verified data type(s). Console display name: "Verified Type(s)".
* `verifyEmail` (string): The email address(es) to be verified for email-verification-required policy. Console display name: "Verification Email Address".
* `verifyPhone` (string): The phone number(s) to be verified for phone-verification-required policy. Console display name: "Verification Phone Number".
* `verifyPolicy` (string): Name of the verify policy. Console display name: "Verify Policy".
* `verifyPolicyId` (string): ID of the verify policy. Console display name: "Verify Policy ID".
* `verifyPolicyIdSelect` (string): ID of the verify policy. Console display name: "Verify Policy ID".
* `verifyPolicySelect` (string): Name of the verify policy. Console display name: "Verify Policy".
* `verifyStatus` (string): Verify status of the user to be set. Console display name: "Verify Status".
* `voiceSampleIndex` (number): voice sample index starting from 1. Console display name: "Voice Sample Index".
* `webVerificationUrl` (string): web verification url. Console display name: "Web Verification URL".


Example:

## Protect

Connector ID (`connector.id` in the resource): `pingOneSnodeRiskConnector`

Properties (used under the `properties` block in the resource as a key in the JSON object):

* `cookie` (string): The cookie of the browser/device that triggered the flow. Console display name: "Cookie".
* `customAttributes` (string): Your Custom Attributes defined at Ping. Console display name: "Custom Attributes".
* `envId` (string): Your Environment ID provided by Ping. Console display name: "Environment ID".
* `externalId` (string): A unique device identifier generated and managed independently of the Signals SDK (SKrisk). Console display name: "External ID".
* `flowType` (string): The type of flow in which risk is evaluated. Console display name: "Flow Type".
* `outcomes` (string): Select the outcomes that are available for this risk evaluation. Defaults to Approve, Deny, and MFA if not specified. Console display name: "Outcomes".
* `riskId` (string): ID of the Risk Evaluation. Console display name: "Risk Evaluation ID".
* `riskPolicySetId` (string): The global risk policy ID used during risk evaluation. Console display name: "Global Policy ID".
* `sessionId` (string): The unique session ID associated with the event. Console display name: "Session ID".
* `showPoweredBy` (string): Console display name: "".
* `skRiskFP` (string): Console display name: "Risk input from device".
* `skipButtonPress` (string): Console display name: "".
* `subtype` (string): The subtype of the flow. Console display name: "Flow Subtype".
* `targetResourceId` (string): The ID for the application or resource the user wants to access. Console display name: "Application ID".
* `targetResourceName` (string): The name of the application or resource the user wants to access. Console display name: "Application Name".
* `targetedPolicy` (boolean): Determines whether the evaluation should automatically select an appropriate policy based on its intended targets, or if a specific policy must be explicitly defined by the user. Console display name: "Targeted Policies Evaluation".
* `userGroups` (string): User groups names. Console display name: "User Groups".
* `userId` (string): The ID of the user whose risk is being evaluated. Console display name: "User ID".
* `userName` (string): The username of the user whose risk is being evaluated. Console display name: "User Name".
* `userType` (string): Indicates whether the user exists in the PingOne directory or in an external directory. Console display name: "User Type".

## Prove International

* `phone` (string):  Formatted in E.164 formatting for international numbers. Console display name: "Phone Number".
* `postalCode` (string): Console display name: "Postal Code".
* `region` (string): Region or State or County. Console display name: "Region".
* `requestId` (string): A unique identifier associated with this request. Console display name: "Request ID".

## SAML IdP

Connector ID (`connector.id` in the resource): `samlIdpConnector`

Properties (used under the `properties` block in the resource as a key in the JSON object):

* `allowUnencryptedAssertion` (string): When enabled, DaVinci accepts SAML assertions from the identity provider that are not encrypted. Only enable this for low-risk transactions in an environment where encryption is not possible. Console display name: "Allow Unencrypted Assertions".
* `audience` (string): The audience value to provide in the SAML request, such as "https://sp.example.com". This value must match one of the audiences listed in the SAML assertion. When this field is blank, the connector uses the DaVinci entity ID. Console display name: "Audience Parameter".
* `authType` (string): Console display name: "".
* `authnContextClassRef` (string): The Context Class Reference to use for the transaction, such as "{ "comparison": "exact", "class_refs": ["urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:ac:classes:Password"] }". This allows you to define the type of authentication required for the transaction. Console display name: "Authentication Context Class Reference".
* `button` (string): Console display name: "Sign On with SAML IdP".
* `forceAuthn` (string): When enabled, the user must re-authenticate even if they have an existing session. Enable this for high-value and high-risk transactions. Console display name: "Force Authentication".
* `nameIdFormat` (string): Select the name format used by the identity provider. Console display name: "".
* `notBeforeSkew` (string): The allowable difference in time between when a SAML assertion becomes valid and the current time, in seconds. Use this to accommodate for differences in clock time between systems. Console display name: "NotBeforeSkew Parameter".
* `relayState` (string): Optional information to include when sending the SAML request to the identity provider, formatted as a URL. This information is included in the response from the identity provider. Console display name: "RelayState Parameter".
* `requireSessionIndex` (string): When enabled, a unique session identifier is carried through the authentication process and allows DaVinci to identify the user's session. Enable this for improved security. Console display name: "".
* `saml` (string): Console display name: "".
* `showPoweredBy` (string): Console display name: "".
* `signRequest` (string): When enabled, DaVinci signs the SAML request using the X.509 certificate. The certificate is provided to the identity provider through the DaVinci SAML SP Metadata URL, which is available in the connector settings. Console display name: "".
* `skipButtonPress` (string): Console display name: "".
* `specificConnectionId` (string): The ID of another DaVinci SAML connector instance, such as "f33f64e40bcf79c2ce86ad0dcc563457". Populate this with a variable to dynamically change which SAML connector is used based on the context of the flow. Console display name: "ID of SAML IdP Connection".


Example:
```terraform
resource "pingone_davinci_connector_instance" "samlIdpConnector" {
  environment_id = var.pingone_environment_id

  connector = {
    id = "samlIdpConnector"
  }
  name = "My awesome samlIdpConnector"
  property {
    name  = "allowUnencryptedAssertion"
    type  = "string"
    value = var.samlidpconnector_property_allow_unencrypted_assertion
  }
  property {
    name  = "audience"
    type  = "string"
    value = var.samlidpconnector_property_audience
  }
  property {
    name  = "authType"
    type  = "string"
    value = var.samlidpconnector_property_auth_type
  }
  property {
    name  = "authnContextClassRef"
    type  = "string"
    value = var.samlidpconnector_property_authn_context_class_ref
  }
  property {
    name  = "button"
    type  = "string"
    value = var.samlidpconnector_property_button
  }
  property {
    name  = "forceAuthn"
    type  = "string"
    value = var.samlidpconnector_property_force_authn
  }
  property {
    name  = "nameIdFormat"
    type  = "string"
    value = var.samlidpconnector_property_name_id_format
  }
  property {
    name  = "notBeforeSkew"
    type  = "string"
    value = var.samlidpconnector_property_not_before_skew
  }
  property {
    name  = "relayState"
    type  = "string"
    value = var.samlidpconnector_property_relay_state
  }
  property {
    name  = "requireSessionIndex"

## SAP Identity API

## SEON

Connector ID (`connector.id` in the resource): `seonConnector`

Properties (used under the `properties` block in the resource as a key in the JSON object):

* `baseURL` (string): The API URL to target. Console display name: "API Base URL".
* `body` (string): The raw JSON body of the API call. Console display name: "Body".
* `endpoint` (string): The SEON API endpoint, such as “SeonRestService/fraud-api/v2.0”. This endpoint is added to the base API URL selected in the connector configuration. Console display name: "Endpoint".
* `fraudScoreConfigType` (string): The configuration type. Can be either Multiselect or JSON. Console display name: "Config Type".
* `fraudScoreJsonConfig` (string): JSON config. Console display name: "Config".
* `fraudScoreMultiSelectConfig` (string): Console display name: "Config".
* `fraudScoreMultiSelectResponseFields` (string): Console display name: "Config Response Fields".
* `headers` (string): Define additional headers to send to SEON. For help, see the SEON REST API documentation. Console display name: "Additional Headers".
* `licenseKey` (string): Your SEON license key. For help, see the SEON REST API documentation. Console display name: "License Key".
* `method` (string): The HTTP method of the API call. Console display name: "HTTP Method".
* `queryParameters` (string): Define additional query parameters to send to SEON. For help, see the SEON REST API documentation. Console display name: "Query Parameters".
* `sendFeedbackTransactions` (string): The list of transactions you want to label with the label texts. Console display name: "Transactions".


Example:
```terraform
resource "pingone_davinci_connector_instance" "seonConnector" {
  environment_id = var.pingone_environment_id

  connector = {
    id = "seonConnector"
  }
  name = "My awesome seonConnector"
  property {
    name  = "baseURL"
    type  = "string"
    value = var.base_url
  }
  property {
    name  = "body"
    type  = "string"
    value = var.seonconnector_property_body
  }
  property {
    name  = "endpoint"
    type  = "string"
    value = var.seonconnector_property_endpoint
  }
  property {
    name  = "fraudScoreConfigType"
    type  = "string"
    value = var.seonconnector_property_fraud_score_config_type
  }
  property {
    name  = "fraudScoreJsonConfig"
    type  = "string"
    value = var.seonconnector_property_fraud_score_json_config
  }
  property {
    name  = "fraudScoreMultiSelectConfig"
    type  = "string"
    value = var.seonconnector_property_fraud_score_multi_select_config
  }
  property {
    name  = "fraudScoreMultiSelectResponseFields"
    type  = "string"
    value = var.seonconnector_property_fraud_score_multi_select_response_fields
  }
  property {
    name  = "headers"
    type  = "string"
    value = var.seonconnector_property_headers
  }
  property {
    name  = "licenseKey"
    type  = "string"
    value = var.seonconnector_property_license_key
  }
  property {
    name  = "method"
    type  = "string"
    value = var.seonconnector_property_method
  }
  property {
    name  = "queryParameters"
    type  = "string"
    value = var.seonconnector_property_query_parameters
  }
  property {
    name  = "sendFeedbackTransactions"
    type  = "string"
    value = var.seonconnector_property_send_feedback_transactions
  }
}
```


## SMTP Client

Connector ID (`connector.id` in the resource): `smtpConnector`

Properties (used under the `properties` block in the resource as a key in the JSON object):

* `email` (string): The comma-separated list of email address to send the message to, such as “jgupta@example.com,dt@example.co.uk”. Console display name: "Recipient".
* `from` (string): The name and email address to show as the sender, such as ““CloudAcme” <registration@cloudacme.com>”. Console display name: "Sender".
* `hostname` (string): Example: smtp-relay.gmail.com. Console display name: "SMTP Server/Host".
* `htmlMessage` (string): The HTML message to send, such as “<h3>Success!</h3><p>Thank you for registering.</p>” This message is used by clients that support HTML. Console display name: "Message (HTML)".
* `message` (string): The plain-text message to send, such as “Success! Thank you for registering.” This message is used by clients that do not support HTML. Console display name: "Message (Plain Text)".
* `name` (string): Optional hostname of the client, used for identifying to the server, defaults to hostname of the machine. Console display name: "Client Name".
* `password` (string): Console display name: "Password".
* `port` (string): Example: 25. Console display name: "SMTP Port".
* `secureFlag` (string): Console display name: "Secure Flag?".
* `sendTestEmail` (string): When enabled, the email is sent using https://ethereal.email instead of your configured SMTP service, for testing purposes. Console display name: "Send Test Email".
* `subject` (string): The subject line for the message, such as “Your account information”. Console display name: "Subject".
* `username` (string): Console display name: "Username".


Example:
```terraform
resource "pingone_davinci_connector_instance" "smtpConnector" {
  environment_id = var.pingone_environment_id

  connector = {
    id = "smtpConnector"
  }
  name = "My awesome smtpConnector"
  property {
    name  = "email"
    type  = "string"
    value = var.smtpconnector_property_email
  }
  property {
    name  = "from"
    type  = "string"
    value = var.smtpconnector_property_from
  }
  property {
    name  = "hostname"
    type  = "string"
    value = var.smtpconnector_property_hostname
  }
  property {
    name  = "htmlMessage"
    type  = "string"
    value = var.smtpconnector_property_html_message
  }
  property {
    name  = "message"
    type  = "string"
    value = var.smtpconnector_property_message
  }
  property {
    name  = "name"
    type  = "string"
    value = var.smtpconnector_property_name
  }
  property {
    name  = "password"
    type  = "string"
    value = var.smtpconnector_property_password
  }
  property {
    name  = "port"
    type  = "string"
    value = var.smtpconnector_property_port
  }
  property {
    name  = "secureFlag"
    type  = "string"
    value = var.smtpconnector_property_secure_flag
  }
  property {
    name  = "sendTestEmail"
    type  = "string"
    value = var.smtpconnector_property_send_test_email
  }
  property {
    name  = "subject"
    type  = "string"
    value = var.smtpconnector_property_subject
  }
  property {
    name  = "username"
    type  = "string"
    value = var.smtpconnector_property_username
  }
}
```


## SailPoint IdentityNow

Connector ID (`connector.id` in the resource): `connectorIdentityNow`

Properties (used under the `properties` block in the resource as a key in the JSON object):

* `accessToken` (string): Access Token from authorization code grant flow (Optional). Console display name: "Access Token".
* `accountName` (string): Requested identity account name. Console display name: "Account Name".
* `apiVersion` (string): The IdentityNow API version ( ex. v3 ). Console display name: "API Version".
* `approvalItemId` (string): Approval Item ID of the IdentityNow request. Console display name: "Approval Item ID ".
* `authMethod` (string): IdentityNow API Authentication Method. Console display name: "API Authentication Method".
* `body` (string): The raw JSON body, such as "{ "Username": "jsmith@example.com", "ProfileId": "00e8a0000024zkjAAA" }". Console display name: "Body".
* `clientId` (string): Client Id for your client found in IdentityNow's Dashboard. Console display name: "Client ID".
* `clientIdPAT` (string): Personal Access Token ID (Optional). Console display name: "Personal Access Token ID".
* `clientSecret` (string): Client Secret from your client in IdentityNow's Dashboard. Console display name: "Client Secret".
* `clientSecretPAT` (string): Personal Access Token Secret (Optional). Console display name: "Personal Access Token Secret".
* `comment` (string): Comment on the approval item. Console display name: "Comment".
* `data` (string): Attribute blob/bag for a non-employee, 10 attributes is the maximum size supported. Console display name: "Data".
* `email` (string): Non-Employee's email. Console display name: "Email".
* `endDate` (string): Non-Employee employment end date. (YYYY-MM-DDThh:mmTZD). Console display name: "End Date".
* `endpoint` (string): The IdentityNow API endpoint, such as "accounts or identity-profiles". Console display name: "Endpoint".
* `familyName` (string): Family Name. Console display name: "Family Name".
* `filters` (string): Filter results using the standard syntax described in V3 API Standard Collection Parameters. Console display name: "Filters".
* `firstName` (string): Non-Employee's first name. Console display name: "First Name".
* `givenName` (string): Given Name. Console display name: "Given Name".
* `headers` (string): Add HTTP headers and provide their values. Console display name: "Headers".
* `lastName` (string): Non-Employee's last name. Console display name: "Last Name".
* `limit` (string): Max number of results to return. Console display name: "Limit".
* `manager` (string): The account ID of a valid identity to serve as this non-employee's manager. Console display name: "Manager".
* `method` (string): The HTTP Method. Console display name: "Method".
* `offset` (string): Offset into the full result set. Console display name: "Offset".
* `phone` (string): Non-Employee's phone. Console display name: "Phone".
* `queryParameters` (string): Add query parameters and provide their values. Console display name: "Query Parameters".
* `showPoweredBy` (string): Console display name: "".
* `skipButtonPress` (string): Console display name: "".
* `sourceId` (string): Non-Employee's source id. Console display name: "Source Id".
* `sourceName` (string): Source Name in IdentityNow. Console display name: "Source Name".
* `startDate` (string): Non-Employee employment start date. Date time format (YYYY-MM-DDThh:mmTZD). Console display name: "Start Date".
* `tenant` (string): The org name is displayed within the Org Details section of the dashboard. Console display name: "IdentityNow Tenant".
* `userId` (string): User ID. Console display name: "User ID".
* `username` (string): Username. Console display name: "Username".

## Salesforce

Connector ID (`connector.id` in the resource): `salesforceConnector`

Properties (used under the `properties` block in the resource as a key in the JSON object):

* `adminUsername` (string): The username of your Salesforce administrator account. Console display name: "Username".
* `alias` (string): The user's alias. Console display name: "Alias".
* `body` (string): The raw JSON body, such as "{ "Username": "jsmith@example.com", "ProfileId": "00e8a0000024zkjAAA" }". Console display name: "Body".
* `consumerKey` (string): The consumer key shown on your Salesforce connected app. Console display name: "Consumer Key".
* `documentDescription` (string): A text description of the document. Console display name: "Description".
* `documentFields` (string): Add document fields and their values. Console display name: "Document Fields".
* `documentFolder` (string): The folder that contains the document. Displays up to 100 results. If the folder you want is not listed, select Use Folder ID. Console display name: "Folder".
* `documentFolderId` (string): The ID of the folder that contains the document, such as  "00l8a000002XKVQAA4". Console display name: "Folder ID".
* `documentKeywords` (string): Searchable keywords to associate with the document. Type a keyword and press Enter to add it. Console display name: "Keywords".
* `documentName` (string): The name of the document. Console display name: "Name".
* `domainName` (string): Your Salesforce domain name, such as "mycompany-dev-ed". Console display name: "Domain Name".
* `email` (string): The user's email address. Console display name: "Email".
* `emailEncodingKey` (string): The email encoding for the user, such as ISO-8859-1 or UTF-8. Console display name: "Email Encoding".
* `endpoint` (string): The Salesforce API endpoint, such as "/services/data/v54.0/sobjects/User". Console display name: "Endpoint".
* `environment` (string): If the environment you specify in the Domain Name field is part of a sandbox organization, select Sandbox. Otherwise, select Production. Console display name: "Environment".
* `file` (string): Base64-encoded file data. Console display name: "File".
* `firstName` (string): The user's first name. Console display name: "First Name".
* `headers` (string): Add HTTP headers and provide their values. Console display name: "Headers".
* `languageLocaleKey` (string): The user’s language, such as French or Chinese (Traditional). Console display name: "Language".
* `lastName` (string): The user's last name. Console display name: "Last Name".
* `localeSidKey` (string): The user's locale. Console display name: "Locale".
* `method` (string): The HTTP Method. Console display name: "Method".
* `nextRecordsUrl` (string): If you expect more than 2000 results, connect multiple Search Record nodes in series. In each node, populate the Next Records URL field with the Next Records URL variable from the previous node. Console display name: "Next Records URL".
* `objectType` (string): The type of standard or custom object, such as "User", "Lead", or "Document". Console display name: "Object Type".
* `privateKey` (string): The private key that corresponds to the X.509 certificate you added to your Salesforce connected app. Console display name: "Private Key".
* `profile` (string): Profiles contain settings and permissions, which control what users can do. Displays up to  100 results. If the profile you want is not listed, select Use Profile ID. Console display name: "Profile".
* `profileId` (string): The ID of the user's profile, such as "00e8a0000024zklAAA". Console display name: "Profile ID".
* `query` (string): Enter a query using Salesforce Object Query Language, such as "SELECT FirstName from User WHERE Id = '0058a00000Ky3eP'". Console display name: "SOQL Query".
* `queryParameters` (string): Add query parameters and provide their values. Console display name: "Query Parameters".
* `recordFieldsRead` (string): Specifies which field values to get for the record. Leave this blank to get all fields. Console display name: "Fields".
* `recordFieldsUpdate` (string): Add the record fields that you want to update and provide their values. Console display name: "Record Fields".
* `recordId` (string): The unique ID of the record, such as "0058a00000LYDB8AAP". Console display name: "Record ID".
* `timeZoneSidKey` (string): The user's timezone. Console display name: "Timezone".
* `userFieldsCreate` (string): Add user fields and their values. Console display name: "User Fields".
* `userFieldsRead` (string): Specifies which field values to get for the user. Leave this blank to get all fields. Console display name: "Fields".
* `userFieldsUpdate` (string): Add the user fields that you want to update and provide their values. Console display name: "User Fields".
* `userId` (string): The unique ID of the user, such as "0058a00000LYDB8AAP". Console display name: "User ID".
* `username` (string): The user's sign-on username, such as "jsmith@example.com". Must be in the form of an email address, using all lowercase characters. It must also be unique across all organizations. Console display name: "Username".

  connector = {
    id = "salesforceConnector"

## Salesforce Marketing Cloud (BETA)

Connector ID (`connector.id` in the resource): `connectorSalesforceMarketingCloud`

Properties (used under the `properties` block in the resource as a key in the JSON object):

* `SalesforceMarketingCloudURL` (string): URL for Salesforce Marketing Cloud. Example: https://YOUR_SUBDOMAIN.rest.marketingcloudapis.com. Console display name: "Salesforce Marketing Cloud URL".
* `Subscribers` (string): Array of up to 250 subscriber records where the message is sent to. Subscribers is different from mobileNumbers. Example - "{ "MobileNumber": "15555554410", "SubscriberKey": "ExampleSubKey1", "Attributes":{ "FirstName": "Michael" } }". Console display name: "Subscribers".
* `accountId` (string): Account identifier, or MID, of the target business unit. Use to switch between business units. If you don’t specify account_id, the returned access token is in the context of the business unit that created the integration. Console display name: "Account ID".
* `attributeSets` (string): Array of information used to create a new contact or update existing contact. Example - "{ "name": "Email Addresses", "items": [{ "values": [{ "name": "Email Address", "value": "acruz@example.com" }, { "name": "HTML Enabled", "value": true }] }] }". Console display name: "Attribute Sets".
* `attributes` (string): The information that personalizes the message for the request, written as key-value pairs. Example - "{ "Purpose": "Sample" }". Console display name: "Attributes".
* `blackoutWindow` (string): Details about the window of time where messages should not be sent. Following values - UtcOffset, WindowStart, WindowEnd. Console display name: "BlackoutWindow".
* `clientId` (string): Client ID issued when you create the API integration in Installed Packages. Console display name: "Client ID".
* `clientSecret` (string): Client secret issued when you create the API integration in Installed Packages. Console display name: "Client Secret".
* `contactKey` (string): Primary address for the contact, such as "acruz@example.com". Change @example.com to a valid domain. Console display name: "Contact Key".
* `contactKeyArray` (string): String array of one or more contact keys. Example - "Key1", "Key2". Console display name: "Contact Keys".
* `content` (string): Content of the SMS. Example - "{ "title": "New Title", "subtitle": "New Subtitle", "message": "This is the overridden message" }". Console display name: "Content".
* `contentURL` (string): The URL of the media content sent via an MMS message. Console display name: "ContentURL".
* `definitionKey` (string): The unique identifier of the definition. Example - "Push Transactional API 1". Console display name: "Definition Key".
* `from` (string): Object containing email address and name of sender. Example - "{ "Address": "code@exacttarget.com", "Name": "Code@" }". Console display name: "From".
* `id` (string): The encoded message ID. Console display name: "Id".
* `keyword` (string): The keyword must align with code on message. Required when subscribe and/or resubscribe are true. Such as - "JOINSMS". Console display name: "Keyword".
* `messageText` (string): Text value to be used in place of the message's original text. This value is required when override is true. Console display name: "Message Text".
* `objectIDorKey` (string): Object ID of the entry event send definition that comes from the response when creating a TriggeredSendDefinition. Either objectID or the external key is required. Console display name: "Object ID or Key".
* `options` (string): Other options. like - { badge: '1' }. Console display name: "Options".
* `optionsASYNCandSYNC` (string): Object used to specify asynchronous or synchronous. If not specified, defaults to asynchronous.  Console display name: "Options".
* `override` (string): Flag to indicate that the contact is receive the messageText as provided instead of the message's original text. True or False. Console display name: "Override".
* `recipients` (string): contains parameters and metadata for the recipient. such as - "{ "contactKey": "recipient1", "messageKey": "f0d8enf0d0snd", "attributes": { "FirstName": "John", "NonRecipientDynamicDefinitionAttribute": "5" } }" or  "{ "to": ["DeviceToken1OfRecipient2", "DeviceToken2OfRecipient2"], "messageKey": "hd846bsbfk037b", "attributes": { "FirstName": "Doe" } }". Console display name: "Recipients".
* `resubscribe` (string): Flag to indicate a subscription should be reset if currently unsubscribed. True or False. Console display name: "Resubscribe".
* `scope` (string): Space-separated list of data-access permissions for your application. Console display name: "Scope".
* `sendTime` (string): Date and Time in UTC that the message will go out. Example format: 2012-10-17 17:01.  Console display name: "Send Time".
* `subscribe` (string): Flag to indicate a subscription should be created if none exist. True or False. Console display name: "Subscribe".
* `to` (string): Object requiring email address and optional subscriber parameters passed in at send time. Example - "{ "Address": "example@example.com", "SubscriberKey": "example@example.com", "ContactAttributes": { "SubscriberAttributes": { "Region": "West", "City": "Indianapolis", "State": "IN" } } }". Console display name: "To".


Example:
```terraform
resource "pingone_davinci_connector_instance" "connectorSalesforceMarketingCloud" {
  environment_id = var.pingone_environment_id

  connector = {
    id = "connectorSalesforceMarketingCloud"
  }
  name = "My awesome connectorSalesforceMarketingCloud"
  property {
    name  = "SalesforceMarketingCloudURL"

## Saviynt Connector Flows

Connector ID (`connector.id` in the resource): `connectorSaviyntFlow`

Properties (used under the `properties` block in the resource as a key in the JSON object):

* `additionalUserProperties` (string): Add other attributes and their values. Console display name: "Other Attributes".
* `advsearchcriteria` (string): search for a user based on the string passed (eg - “*ab*” or “*ab” or “ab*”), example - {"username":"a*", "firstname":"*b"} - This will return all users with username starting with "a" AND firstname ending with "b". Exact match search is applicable for types boolean, users, customer. Date can be entered in format - yyyy-MM-dd. Console display name: "Advance Search Criteria".
* `city` (string): Provide your city name. Console display name: "City".
* `comments` (string): Comments by approver for particular request. Console display name: "Comments".
* `companyname` (string): Provide your company name. Console display name: "Company Name".
* `country` (string): Provide your country name. Console display name: "Country".
* `designation` (string): Provide designation. Console display name: "Designation".
* `domainName` (string): Provide your Saviynt domain name. Console display name: "Saviynt Domain Name".
* `email` (string): Email of the user. Console display name: "Email".
* `employeeType` (string): Employee Type of the user. Console display name: "`Employee Type".
* `enabled` (string): To enable disable the user. Console display name: "Enabled".
* `enddate` (string): Provide last date of the user. Console display name: "End Date".
* `filtercriteria` (string): User fields based on which you want to get the user attribute details(including userkey). Console display name: "Filter Criteria".
* `firstname` (string): First Name of the user. Console display name: "First Name".
* `lastname` (string): Last Name of the user. Console display name: "Last Name".
* `manager` (string): Manager of the user. Console display name: "Manager".
* `max` (string): Maximum number of requests. Console display name: "Maximum number of requests".
* `middlename` (string): Provide your middle name. Console display name: "Middle Name".
* `name` (string): Provide your name. Console display name: "Name".
* `offset` (string): Offset. Console display name: "Offset".
* `order` (string):  asc/desc. Console display name: "Order".
* `path` (string): Provide your Saviynt path name. Console display name: "Saviynt Path Name".
* `phonenumber` (string): Provide your phone number. Console display name: "Phone Number".
* `rank` (string): Provide rank. Console display name: "Rank".
* `reqaction` (string): it will take the value either 1 or 2 for approve/reject respectively. Console display name: "Request Action".
* `requestKey` (string): Request Key of the pending request. Console display name: "Request Key".
* `requestid` (string): Request ID of pending request to approve/reject. Console display name: "Request ID".
* `responsefields` (string): User attributes which you want to see in the response. Console display name: "Response Fields".
* `rolename` (string): Provide a role name. Console display name: "Role Name".
* `roles` (string): Roles of the user. Console display name: "Roles".
* `saviyntPassword` (string): Provide your Saviynt password. Console display name: "Saviynt Password".
* `saviyntUserName` (string): Provide your Saviynt user name. Console display name: "Saviynt User Name".
* `searchCriteria` (string): search for a user based on the string passed (eg - “*ab*” or “*ab” or “ab*”) in their firstname, lastname, displayname and username only, example - "ab*" - This will return all users with firstname or lastname or username starting with "ab". Console display name: "Search Criteria".
* `showsecurityanswers` (string): True / false to display encrypted security answers for the user. Console display name: "Show Security Answers".
* `sort` (string): Sort. Console display name: "Sort".
* `startdate` (string): Start Date of the user. Console display name: "Start Date".
* `state` (string): Provide your state name. Console display name: "State".
* `status` (string): Status of the user. Console display name: "Status".
* `statuskey` (string): Statuskey of the user. Console display name: "StatusKey".
* `systemusername` (string): System username of the user. Console display name: "System Username".
* `type` (string): Provide type. Console display name: "Type".
* `username` (string): username for the create user. Console display name: "Username".
* `value` (string): Provide value. Console display name: "Value".

## Secret Double Octopus

Connector ID (`connector.id` in the resource): `secretDoubleOctopusConnector`

Properties (used under the `properties` block in the resource as a key in the JSON object):

* `apiToken` (string): The 128-character API Token found in the Management Console under Service > Sign-On tab. Console display name: "API Token".
* `authId` (string): The authId returned from Create Authentication Request, used to poll for status. Console display name: "Authentication ID".
* `baseUrl` (string): The root URL of your Secret Double Octopus authentication server (e.g., https://sdo.example.com). Console display name: "Base URL".
* `message` (string): Custom message displayed to the user during authentication (optional). Console display name: "Push Message".
* `password` (string): Password for authentication. Console display name: "Password".
* `serviceId` (string): The service UUID found in the REST Endpoint URL field in the Management Console under Service > Sign-On tab. Console display name: "Service ID".
* `username` (string): Username for authentication. Console display name: "Username".
* `x509Certificate` (string): The public certificate from SDO used to verify response signatures, found in the Management Console under Service > Sign-On tab. Console display name: "X.509 Certificate".

## SecurID

Connector ID (`connector.id` in the resource): `securIdConnector`

Properties (used under the `properties` block in the resource as a key in the JSON object):

* `apiUrl` (string): The URL of your SecurID authentication API, such as "https://company.auth.securid.com". Console display name: "SecurID Authentication API REST URL".
* `assurancePolicyId` (string): The name of your SecurID policy, such as "All Users Low Assurance Level". Console display name: "Assurance Policy Name".
* `authnAttemptTimeout` (string): A number in seconds representing how long the server will keep the authentication attempt ID available after each call. During this time is is possible to make other calls using the "authnAttemptId". The server may reject initialization requests if the value provided is beyond the allowable maximum. Defaults to a server-defined session lifetime. Optional. Console display name: "Authentication Attempt Timeout".
* `clientKey` (string): Your SecurID authentication client key, such as "vowc450ahs6nry66vok0pvaizwnfr43ewsqcm7tz". Console display name: "Client Key".
* `htmlConfig0` (string): Console display name: "".
* `htmlConfig1` (string): Console display name: "".
* `htmlConfig2` (string): Console display name: "".
* `keepAttempt` (string): When enabled, SecurID keeps a record of each completed transaction. Console display name: "Keep Record".
* `subjectName` (string): The unique identifier for the user, such as an email, account name, user ID. Console display name: "User Identifier".

  }
  property {

  property {

This parameter is optional.Enter true to receive the list of child cases associated with a parent case in the response. Otherwise, enter false. This parameter is optional. Console display name: "Allow Child Cases".

* `eventTimeTo` (string): Enter the event time end range in format MM/dd/yyyy HH:mm:ss. Console display name: "Event Time To".

## Segment

Connector ID (`connector.id` in the resource): `connectorSegment`

Properties (used under the `properties` block in the resource as a key in the JSON object):

* `body` (string): The raw custom JSON body. Console display name: "Body".
* `endpoint` (string): Use an HTTP Tracking API endpoint, such as "identify, track, page, screen, group, or alias". Console display name: "Endpoint".
* `genericProperties` (string): Any desired descriptive attribute(s). Console display name: "Properties".
* `genericTraits` (string): Any desired descriptive attribute(s). Console display name: "Traits".
* `groupId` (string): Unique identifier which you recognize a group by. Console display name: "Group ID".
* `headers` (string): Add HTTP headers and provide their values. Console display name: "Headers".
* `method` (string): The HTTP Method. Console display name: "Method".
* `pageName` (string): Name of the page - Reserved for future use. Console display name: "Page Name".
* `previousId` (string): The existing ID you've referred to this user by. Console display name: "Previous User ID".
* `queryParameters` (string): Key-value pairs that are used to define any desired characteristics about a certain endpoint call. Console display name: "Traits / Properties".
* `screenName` (string): Name of the screen from a mobile device - Reserved for future use. Console display name: "Screen Name".
* `userEvent` (string): Name of the action that the user has performed. Console display name: "Event".
* `userId` (string): Unique identifier for the user. Console display name: "User ID".
* `version` (string): Segment - HTTP Tracking API Version. Console display name: "HTTP Tracking API Version".
* `writeKey` (string): The Write Key is used to send data to a specific workplace. Console display name: "Write Key".

## SentinelOne

Connector ID (`connector.id` in the resource): `sentineloneConnector`

Properties (used under the `properties` block in the resource as a key in the JSON object):

* `apiKey` (string): The SentinelOne API token. Paste only the raw token value. Console display name: "API Token".
* `baseUrl` (string): The root URL of your SentinelOne Management Console (e.g., https://usea1-partners.sentinelone.net). Console display name: "Base URL".
* `serialNumber` (string): The full hardware serial number of the device to look up. An exact match is required — partial serial numbers will not return an agent. Console display name: "Serial Number".


Example:
```terraform
resource "pingone_davinci_connector_instance" "sentineloneConnector" {
  environment_id = var.pingone_environment_id

  }
  name = "My awesome sentineloneConnector"

  }
  property {
    name  = "baseUrl"
